articles.title: Clayface's Tom Rhys Harries says prosthetics helped performance
articles.summary: Tom Rhys Harries says he spent half his time on set with the make-up team.
articles.body:
Actors are often said to be the face of the film, but in Tom Rhys Harries' breakout role in DC's latest blockbuster, that part of the body becomes the focal point to chart the character's descent into villainy.

Rhys Harries plays the lead in Clayface as Matt Hagen - a handsome, successful actor.

When his face is mutilated in an attack, he volunteers for trials of a new treatment with horrifying side effects that transform his face into living clay.

The Welsh actor said he spent about half of his time on the set with the special effects make-up team, transforming into the mutant villain.

Despite the difficulty of wearing extensive prosthetics during filming, Rhys Harries said it helped him portray the distress of his character in a film that has been described as a body horror psychological thriller.

"There was a benefit to having it, because the character is in discomfort," he said.

Clayface first appeared in DC comics in 1940 as a Batman villain, however the character has never been adapted for cinema, until now, and it is the first major studio movie role for Rhys Harries.

"Time will tell if I'm prepared for it," the Cardiff-born actor said.

"I think it feels like a real privilege to be allowed into that sandbox, it's a cultural thing that is fairly significant in the West certainly.

"So I just feel really grateful to be able to put my stamp on Matt and Clayface for the first time."

Where possible, the creative team used malleable physical effects to better reflect the consistency of a clay-like substance, something Rhys Harries said was a "steep learning curve".

"You've got these artists who've created this piece of work that happens to be on you and the inclination is not ruin their work, but this stuff really works when you're able to interact with it.

"Because you would - if there was something on you that was mutating or morphing - you would go to touch it."

The film is described as a body horror psychological thriller, but Rhys Harries insists the story is relatable.

"He's an actor who happens to have lost one of his tools and it would be much the same as if a violinist had lost the use of his hands.

"It's just what any of us would do where your means of making a living has been taken away and I think there's a relatability in that."

Rhys Harries, who has been acting professionally for the past 15 years in English and Welsh, believes Welsh cultural traditions have played a part in his success.

"I was taking part in the Eisteddfod when I was five and doing recitals in front of two, 300 people, so it didn't feel alien to me to be pursuing a career within that field.

"And I think that's a great strength of us as a nation, our cultural output.

"It's fairly ridiculous given the size of the country how impactful I think we are on a global stage, culturally, and I think that's something we should foster within Wales."

articles.title: 'Fostering saved my life,' says Bristol care leaver
articles.summary: A woman says fostering "saved her life" as a campaign launches to tackle a shortage of carers.
articles.body:
A woman who entered care at 14 says her foster parents gave her stability, love and a future she never thought possible.

The number of foster carers has fallen by 12% since 2021 while the number of children needing care continues to rise.

The government has initiated a campaign to get 10,000 more foster care places. Ministers are promoting regional fostering hubs set up in recent years, including in the South West.

"Fostering definitely saved my life. If I wasn't fostered I don't know who I'd have ended up with," said Amy Burns, who was there for the launch at Downing Street.

'Lifeline' swimming group celebrating 50 years

Closures highlight struggles facing local theatres

In Pictures: 'Lido's dog event' and 'world BBQ finalists'

Amy, now 26, and from Bristol, entered foster care at the age of 14 after what she describes as a difficult family situation.

Looking back, she believes the support and stability she received changed the course of her life.

"I had come out of a really bad family relationship, and if I hadn't been actually saved by my foster parents, I don't know where I'd have ended up.

"If they didn't stick it out, and if they didn't give me the love that I needed then I absolutely would not be here today."

Amy went on to attend university and build a career in the media, something she says would not have been possible without her foster family.

Amy's story comes as foster carer numbers fall and demand for placements grows.

The number of children in care in Bristol and Somerset has risen by 35% over the past seven years.

Experts say foster care often delivers better outcomes for children, but a shortage of carers means more young people are ending up in children's homes.

Amy was among the speakers at the launch of a new government initiative aimed at recruiting thousands more foster carers.

The campaign includes a push to attract people from a wider range of backgrounds and encourage more flexible forms of fostering.

Children and Families Minister Josh MacAlister said more people may now be able to consider fostering.

"Families can come forward in their 20s or 30s or 40s, who might be able to foster part-time at the weekends," he said.

"Now is the time to come forward and join fostering, because it is changing and it is improving."

Guidelines will be made clearer, helped by £88m of new funding.

'People talk themselves out of fostering'

Also backing the campaign is Wes, a single parent from Yate in South Gloucestershire, who has fostered and adopted children over the past 14 years.

Wes, 46, believes many people rule themselves out before finding out what fostering involves.

"I feel that every day I've made a chance for a child to have a better life," he said.

He said concerns about finances or the challenges children may bring should not necessarily stop people from applying.

"Yes there is trauma, and yes sometimes I have to talk about the past, but to me it's all about the day that you're in and what's coming forward, that child knows that they're going to be safe and happy in my care."

Among those supporting recruitment efforts is Jon Hubbard, Wiltshire Council's cabinet member for children's services.

His council plays a leading role in the South West Fostering Hub, which was set up two years ago to help councils work together on recruitment and support for foster carers.

He said the shortage of foster homes had practical as well as financial consequences because more children end up in residential care, where placements can be significantly more expensive - at £318,000 per year.

"I cannot stress enough: every foster carer we recruit not only makes a massive difference to a young person's life, but also actually saves a considerable amount of money," he said.

articles.title: Met Police says it received 2019 letter with claims about Meghan’s father but didn’t share it with other agencies
articles.summary: London police confirmed they received a 2019 letter with claims about Meghan’s father and passed it to her office without sharing it with other agencies.
articles.body:
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, said she is "deeply distressed" by the news that her father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation over claims he possessed images containing child sexual abuse in his home.

The images were reportedly found in his home in the Philippines after he returned to the U.S. in May, Philippine officials said.

Thomas Markle denied the allegations, calling them "sick lies" and "the worst thing anyone could accuse me of."

London's Metropolitan Police confirmed Saturday that it received a letter in January 2019 containing "a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom," the BBC reported . The letter was sent to the force's protection command because of concerns about the duchess's security.

The Met said it passed the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex "for their awareness," but did not share the details with other law enforcement agencies. The force said it is reviewing how it handled the matter and considering whether to refer itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct, the police watchdog.

In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan Markle said that she is "deeply distressed" by the news, and that she was first made aware of the claims by the Met Police in 2018.

"I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," Meghan's statement said. "In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.

"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.

"I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.

"Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."

Meghan had said the letter was sent in 2018. A spokesman for the duchess said Saturday that "any discrepancy of a few months" was "an understandable consequence of that passage of time."

Authorities in the Philippines are also investigating. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said national police had secured Markle's computer for a forensic examination, the BBC reported.

The allegations, reported by Mail Online , said Thomas Markle is under investigation after being reported by his son, Thomas Markle Jr.

In a statement to Mail Online , the elder Markle said: "I'm shocked, I'm hurt and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of."

He added: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick. I have no idea why Tom [Markle] is trying to destroy me with these lies."

Yahoo has contacted the Met Office and authorities in the U.S. and the Philippines for comment.

articles.title: What’s Delhi breathing? IITM’s new lab decodes air mix
articles.summary: IITM’s new Delhi lab AATAL provides real-time PM2.5 source apportionment: vehicles top at 25%, followed by secondary aerosols; aids targeted action.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vehicles were the single largest contributor to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution Saturday, accounting for 25%, according to data generated by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology’s (IITM) newly inaugurated Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL). Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4%, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5%), road dust (10.9%) and waste burning (5%).The laboratory, which provides real-time source-apportionment data, was inaugurated in New Rajendra Nagar by Union minister of state Jitendra Singh Saturday. Equipped with 25 advanced instruments and built at an estimated instrument cost of Rs 79.5 crore, the facility is designed to identify pollutants, trace their sources, understand how they transform in the atmosphere and assess their potential health impacts.AATAL will complement IITM’s existing Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS), which provides AQI forecasts, and the Decision Support System (DSS), which estimates the contribution of local and regional pollution sources. A revamped EWS was also launched.Officials said the laboratory would strengthen research on the interaction of aerosols with moisture, fog and haze, particularly during winter in northern India.Data generated over the past five days show that vehicles, secondary organic aerosols and secondary inorganic aerosols have consistently been the top contributors to Delhi’s PM2.5 levels, although their shares have varied.On Friday, when Delhi’s AQI was in the poor category, secondary organic aerosols were the largest contributor at 24.6%, while vehicles and secondary inorganic aerosols each accounted for 20.7%. Road dust remained a significant contributor, accounting for 5-10% of PM2.5 in recent days.Secondary organic aerosols form when volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released by vehicles, industries, solvents and vegetation react in the atmosphere to form particulate matter. Secondary inorganic aerosols are formed through chemical reactions involving gases such as sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and ammonia, producing sulphates and nitrates.Singh said, “Earlier, the discussion would largely revolve around whether the pollution level was 100 or 200. This facility will help us understand the composition of pollution as well as the contribution of different sources. This ensures that action is based on scientific evidence.”He added that the facility would provide insights into the smaller constituents of air pollution, including metallic elements and other potentially harmful components. Understanding not only pollutant concentrations but also their composition and toxicity was important because different pollutants could have different health impacts, he said.Sachin Ghude, project director, said the initial findings show that around 40% of Delhi’s PM2.5 is primary particulate matter, while 60% is secondary. “Unlike primary particles, which are emitted directly into the air, secondary aerosols form when gases undergo chemical reactions in the atmosphere and get converted into particles. The findings indicate that primary particles, secondary inorganic aerosols and secondary organic aerosols each account for around 30% of the total PM2.5, while the remaining 10% comprises metals, toxic elements and other components,” he told TOI.The facility restores real-time source-apportionment data for Delhi after a gap of nearly three years. The previous system operated by IIT Kanpur ceased in Nov 2023 after Delhi govt halted the project. Officials said the initiative would now be resumed with the help of IIT Delhi.The laboratory is expected to support the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and other agencies in identifying major pollution sources, prioritising interventions and assessing their effectiveness. articles.summary: Reportagens incluem rato flagrado 'tomando banho', sabatina com Alan Rick, marido que doou rim para esposa, homenagens a Ayres Rocha e mais.
articles.body:
Confira o que foi destaque no g1 AC entre 18 a 24 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: g1 AC

O g1 lista as reportagens mais acessadas para você ficar por dentro de tudo que aconteceu entre 18 e 24 de outubro. Confira abaixo.

Uma cena inusitada surpreendeu a pedagoga Cléia Rodrigues Machado, de 45 anos, na sua casa em Rio Branco . Ela flagrou um rato tomando banho no tanque de sua lavanderia nesse domingo (18). ( Veja acima )

Nas imagens, o animal com o corpo molhado, dentro da água acumulada no tanque. Ele esfrega o corpo e a cabeça, em movimentos que lembram os hábitos de higiene humana no banho. Após compartilhar as imagens na internet, Cleia informou que o vídeo já ultrapassou 100 mil visualizações.

Ela contou que se deparou com a cena por volta das 9h30, quando foi até a área de serviço para lavar um uniforme do filho que estava de molho desde a noite de sábado (17). Contudo, ao chegar ao tanque, ela levou um susto com a presença do animal e decidiu registrar o momento. Segundo Cleia, o rato fugiu após o cachorro da família latir.

🩹 O amor e a parceria de 15 anos ganharam um novo significado para o casal Elaine Aparecida Silva Leal, de 40 anos, e Luiz Miguel Pereira, de 43. É que após anos convivendo com a doença renal crônica (DRC) da esposa, Luiz conseguiu realizou o desejo de doar um rim para ela.

A operação ocorreu no último sábado (17), na Fundação Hospitalar Governador Flaviano Melo (Fundhacre), em Rio Branco. O procedimento marcou o segundo transplante renal intervivos feito no Acre em 2026 em menos de dois meses. O primeiro foi do adolescente Lucas Linhares, de 14 anos.

Conforme Elaine, a descoberta da doença renal começou no início do relacionamento com Luiz, em 2011. Ao longo de 15 anos de casados, o esposo acompanhou de perto os desafios impostos pelo tratamento de Elaine, que passou a incluir sessões de hemodiálise em agosto de 2024.

A família de Willian Silva de Oliveira, de 32 anos, que morreu após receber uma descarga elétrica durante a enchente de março de 2024, na zona rural de Capixaba , interior do Acre, deve receber uma indenização de R$ 110 mil da concessionária Energisa.

A Justiça manteve, na última terça-feira (20), a condenação da empresa ao pagamento por danos morais à companheira e aos dois filhos dele, além de uma pensão mensal. A decisão prevê R$ 40 mil para a esposa e R$ 35 mil para cada um dos dois filhos menores do casal.

A pensão mensal foi fixada em R$ 470,66, dividida igualmente entre os três beneficiários. A família também deve receber as parcelas atrasadas desde a morte de Willian, com correção monetária pelo INPC e juros de mora.

Uma situação inusitada chamou a atenção de moradores de Cruzeiro do Sul , interior do Acre, na manhã de terça-feira (20). É que um homem de 26 anos foi encontrado dormindo no topo de um telão de LED usado para publicidade, a 6 metros do chão, na Praça Orleir Cameli, no Centro. (Veja vídeo acima)

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado para fazer o resgate. Para retirar o homem da estrutura, as equipes de salvamento e de combate a incêndio isolaram a área e iniciaram a operação com técnicas de salvamento em altura e equipamentos de segurança.

Ao g1 , o Corpo de Bombeiros informou que o homem, morador do bairro do Formoso, subiu na estrutura por medo de sofrer agressões de outras pessoas. A Polícia Militar (PM-AC) também foi acionada para atender à ocorrência.

😍📺 Microfone na mão, crachá no peito e o olhar de quem está pronto para entrar no ar. Aos 12 anos, Davi Luiz Lopes Ribeiro já sabe bem o que quer ser quando pega seu microfone e começa a imitar um apresentador de telejornal.

Fã de jornalismo desde pequeno, ele escolheu uma figura especial para representar no Dia da Fantasia: o jornalista Ayres Rocha, que morreu aos 62 anos no último dia 14 , em Rio Branco, após complicações de um câncer. A missa de sétimo dia do jornalista ocorreu na última terça-feira (20), na Catedral Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, no Centro da capital, às 19h.

A homenagem aconteceu durante uma atividade da semana da criança, na quinta (15), dia em que o corpo do apresentador foi enterrado . A fantasia já estava preparada antes de a família saber da notícia, e Davi foi vestido como apresentador do Jornal do Acre 2ª edição (JAC2) para representar o jornalista que ele acompanhava desde pequeno.

O candidato ao governo do Acre Alan Rick (Republicanos) foi entrevistado pela Rede Amazônica Acre na última quinta-feira (22). A sabatina foi transmitida ao vivo pela emissora e pelo g1 , com apresentação do jornalista Fabiano Villela da TV Globo.

A Rede Amazônica promoveria um debate entre os postulantes a chefe do Executivo acreano, mas a candidata a reeleição Mailza Assis (PP) cancelou a participação devido a compromissos de campanha na regional do Alto Acre , mais especificamente em Brasiléia e Epitaciolândia , no interior, que estavam previamente agendados.

Alan foi questionado sobre temas como educação e saúde, além de segurança, infraestrutura e bioeconomia, em um período de 20 minutos. Confira na íntegra aqui.

articles.title: Eleições: centro-oeste de SP vota para presidente no 2º turno  | G1
articles.standfirst: Neste segundo turno, os eleitores no estado votam apenas para presidente. Mais de 1 milhão de eleitores estão aptos a votar nas 100 cidades do centro-oeste paulista.
articles.summary: Mais de 1 milhão de eleitores do centro-oeste de SP votam para presidente neste domingo, incluindo quem não compareceu às urnas no primeiro turno das eleições.
articles.body:
Neste domingo (25), mais de 1 milhão de eleitores aptos a votar neste segundo turno no centro-oeste paulista devem ir às urnas para eleger o presidente. A votação ocorre das 8 às 17h e no estado de São Paulo, os eleitores votam apenas para presidente neste segundo turno.

Nas cinco maiores cidades do centro-oeste paulista - Bauru , Marília , Botucatu , Jaú e Ourinhos - são quase 740 mil eleitores aptos e destes, pouco mais de 172 mil não compareceram às urnas no primeiro turno, uma abstenção média de 22% considerando a soma das cidades.

No primeiro turno, a abstenção em Bauru, maior colégio eleitoral da região com 278.336 eleitores, foi de 25,11%, o que corresponde a quase 70 mil eleitores (69.900). Isso significa que um a cada quatro eleitores não votou no primeiro turno na cidade.

O índice supera, inclusive, abstenção no país, que foi de 21,6%, totalizando 33 milhões de eleitores que não foram às urnas. O número de abstenção na cidade também é o maior se comparado às eleições de 2022, que teve 63.917 eleitores ausentes, representando 22,86% da quantidade de aptos a votar daquele ano, que era de 279.646.

Mesmo quem não votou no primeiro turno está apto para votar neste segundo. A justificativa para ausência no primeiro turno pode ser feita até o dia 3 de dezembro.

No segundo turno, essa data é estendida até 8 de janeiro de 2027. Caso não haja justificativa, o eleitor pagará uma multa de R$ 3,51 por turno perdido .

Primeiro turno teve filas pontuais em alguns locais de votação em Bauru — Foto: TV TEM/Raissa Toledo

Em Marília, a abstenção foi de 23,43% do total de eleitores aptos que são 172.936 na cidade, ou seja, 40.520 deixaram de votar no primeiro turno.

Já em Botucatu, dos 111.048 eleitores aptos, 25.320 não compareceram, uma abstenção de 22,8%.

Em Jaú, 18.973 eleitores não votaram no primeiro turno, o que corresponde a 19,22% do total do eleitorado, que é de 98.725 eleitores.

Dos 76.480 eleitores de Ourinhos, 17.800 não foram às urnas no primeiro turno, somando uma abstenção de 23,27%.

Segundo turno das eleições 2026 será realizado neste domingo — Foto: TSE

Mesmo que não tenha foto, o aplicativo ajuda a encontrar o local de votação rapidamente, assim como a versão em papel.

Para o voto, o TSE exige a apresentação de um documento com foto, o que, além do e-Título, inclui carteira de identidade, identidade social, carteira de trabalho, carteira nacional de habilitação, passaporte ou equivalente, carteira de categoria profissional reconhecida por lei ou certificado de reservista.

articles.standfirst: Votação ocorre neste domingo (25), das 8h às 17h. Saiba quais documentos levar, o que é proibido na cabine, a ordem de votação e se quem faltou no 1º turno pode votar agora.
articles.summary: Eleitores de Rio Preto e Araçatuba votam neste domingo (25) no segundo turno das Eleições 2026. Veja guia com principais dúvidas e informações para a votação.
articles.body:
Urnas eletrônicas começam a ser levadas para locais de votação em Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: André Modesto/TV TEM

Os eleitores de São José do Rio Preto e Araçatuba (SP) voltam às urnas neste domingo (25) para o segundo turno das Eleições 2026. Na votação, os eleitores vão escolher entre os dois candidatos que disputam a Presidência da República: Lula ( PT ) ou Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ).

Para garantir que o momento do voto seja rápido e sem imprevistos, o g1 preparou um guia prático com as principais orientações da Justiça Eleitoral.

✅ Não votei no 1º turno, posso votar no 2º?

Sim. A Justiça Eleitoral considera cada turno como uma eleição independente. Quem não compareceu ou ainda não justificou a ausência no primeiro turno pode e deve votar normalmente no segundo turno , desde que o título de eleitor esteja em situação regular.

A ausência no primeiro tur ainda deve ser justificada formalmente no prazo legal de até 60 dias após a data do 1º turno.

No estado de São Paulo, a escolha será para apenas um cargo: o de presidente da República (2 dígitos). Basta digitar os dois dígitos do candidato escolhido, conferir a foto na tela e apertar a tecla confirma.

As seções eleitorais abrem às 8h e encerram as atividades às 17h (horário de Brasília). Eleitores que chegarem à fila até as 17h recebem senha para registrar o voto normalmente.

Sim. A Justiça Eleitoral incentiva que o eleitor leve anotado em papel o número do seu candidato para digitar rapidamente na urna.

💷 Quais documentos são aceitos para votar?

Não é obrigatório apresentar o título impresso, mas é obrigatório apresentar um documento oficial com foto. São válidos:

Carteira de Identidade (RG) ou Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN);

⚠ Uso do e-Título: O aplicativo substitui os documentos físicos apenas para quem já cadastrou a biometria e tem a foto visível na tela inicial. Sem foto no app, é exigido um documento físico oficial com foto. (O download e a atualização do e-Título só podem ser feitos até as 23h59 de sábado, véspera do pleito).

📴 É permitido entrar com celular na cabine de votação?

Não. O uso de celulares, máquinas fotográficas, filmadoras ou qualquer equipamento de comunicação é proibido na cabine para preservar o sigilo do voto . O aparelho deve ficar desligado e entregue aos mesários da mesa receptora antes do eleitor se dirigir à urna eletrônica.

É permitido comparecer ao local de votação de bermuda, calça, chinelo, camiseta ou regata. É vedada a entrada sem camisa ou com trajes de banho (como biquíni e sunga).

Posso ir com a camiseta do meu candidato? A manifestação individual e silenciosa da preferência política por meio de broches, adesivos, bandeiras e camisetas com fotos ou nomes de candidatos é permitida.

Aglomerações de pessoas vestindo camisas ou padronagens idênticas (configurando manifestação coletiva), distribuição de brindes ou propaganda eleitoral e a abordagem de outros eleitores para pedir voto (boca de urna).

🏫 Onde eu voto? Como consultar meu local de votação e minha seção eleitoral?

Antes de sair para votar, o eleitor deve consultar o local de votação, pois pode haver alteração desde as últimas eleições. A consulta ao local de votação pode ser feita por meio do site do Autoatendimento eleitoral ou pelo aplicativo e-Título.

No site, é necessário clicar em “Onde Votar”, menu “Consultas”, preencher os dados solicitados e inserir o código de autenticação do e-Título. Pelo aplicativo, basta fazer login, por meio da biometria e, então, escolher a aba “Onde votar”. É possível copiar o endereço no mapa ou abri-lo em aplicativo de mobilidade para conferir as rotas disponíveis até o local.

🚗 Solicitei voto em trânsito. Como verificar onde votar?

Quem solicitou o voto em trânsito deverá votar no local de votação para o qual foi transferido. Não será possível votar na seção original. Caso a pessoa não esteja no município para o qual se transferiu, será possível justificar a ausência normalmente. É possível votar em trânsito em cidades distintas nos dois turnos. O retorno para o local de votação original após a eleição ocorre de forma automática.

Sim. Desde que o título esteja em situação regular, a pessoa sem biometria que comparecer à seção eleitoral com um documento oficial com foto poderá votar normalmente. Mesmo quem não fez a coleta dos dados biométricos poderá ser habilitado por meio da digital. Isso ocorre porque a Justiça Eleitoral tem parceria com outros órgãos para importar a biometria para o sistema de votação, permitindo que esse grupo vote com a identificação biométrica.

O transporte coletivo vai funcionar com horário especial no domingo em Rio Preto. O embarque será gratuito para os moradores em todas as linhas, sem limite de uso. Os ônibus irão circular com a mesma frequência dos dias úteis. Para conferir os horários e as linhas de ônibus, basta acessar o site da empresa.

O eleitor que estiver fora de seu domicílio eleitoral pode justificar:

No domingo de votação: preferencialmente pelo aplicativo e-Título (que detecta a localização geográfica fora da cidade) ou entregando o formulário impresso de justificativa em qualquer seção eleitoral, das 8h às 17h.

Após o dia da votação: em até 60 dias por meio do aplicativo e-Título, pelo portal do TSE ou diretamente no cartório eleitoral com a documentação comprobatória da ausência.

♿ As urnas eletrônicas possuem recursos de acessibilidade?

Sim. O teclado numérico possui teclas com sensibilidade tátil e marcação em Braille, além de ser disposto na mesma ordem dos telefones para facilitar a identificação. Para eleitores com deficiência auditiva ou visual, o equipamento oferece saída para fone de ouvido, sintetizador de voz que lê as teclas digitadas e os nomes dos candidatos e intérprete de Libras na tela para orientar sobre os cargos e a confirmação do voto, indicando o voto em branco, nulo e no partido.

articles.title: Quase 7 milhões de eleitores no Ceará estão aptos a votar no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Cearenses vão às urnas para escolher entre o atual presidente Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Eleição para governador do Ceará já foi definida no primeiro turno.
articles.summary: Cearenses vão às urnas para escolher entre o atual presidente Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Eleição para governador do Ceará já foi definida no primeiro turno.
articles.body:
Quase 7 milhões de eleitores no Ceará estão aptos a votar neste domingo (25), segundo turno da eleição para presidente da República em 2026.

Brasileiros vão às urnas mais uma vez em 2026 para escolher entre o atual presidente Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Como a eleição para governador no Ceará já foi definida em primeiro turno , os cearenses irão votar agora apenas para o cargo de presidente.

São exatos 6.996.521 eleitores em todo o estado que estão aptos a votar neste segundo turno das Eleições 2026 . Isso significa 1.973 pessoas a menos em relação ao primeiro turno, quando 6.998.494 podiam participar da votação no Ceará.

Conforme o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Ceará (TRE-CE), a diferença é em razão das Transferências Temporárias de Eleitor (TTE).

➡️A Transferência Temporária de Eleitora/Eleitor - TTE é a transferência, em um pleito específico, para votar em seção eleitoral diferente da seção de origem. Nas Eleições 2026 está facultada a TTE no primeiro, no segundo ou em ambos os turnos. Para a TTE ser realizada, as eleitoras e os eleitores devem estar com a situação regular no Cadastro Eleitoral, segundo o site do TRE-CE.

Para votar, o eleitor deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto aos mesários. O título de eleitor em papel não é obrigatório. Também é possível votar usando apenas o aplicativo e-Título , desde que ele exiba a fotografia do eleitor. O aplicativo é a versão digital do título de eleitor e reúne informações e serviços da Justiça Eleitoral.

🗳️ Em 2026, os brasileiros votam para os cargos de presidente da República, governador do Estado, senadores, deputados federais e deputados estaduais. Nos casos dos chefes dos Executivos nacional e estadual, pode ocorrer segundo turno quando nenhum dos candidatos consegue a maioria absoluta dos votos válidos.

Para ajudar no deslocamento de eleitores até os locais de votação, há mudanças no transporte público em diversas cidades. Em Fortaleza, os ônibus vão funcionar gratuitamente e com reforço na frota .

Além disso, este domingo é considerado feriado nacional com a eleição. Assim, o funcionamento de alguns serviços e estabelecimentos foram alterados. Confira o que abre e o que fecha em Fortaleza neste domingo.

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) se enfrentam no 2º turno da eleição para presidente da República — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Vara e REUTERS/Pilar Olivares

O Ceará registrou a menor abstenção do Brasil na votação do primeiro turno das Eleições 2026 , no último dia 4 de outubro. O índice de abstenção foi de 15,53%, abaixo do nacional, que foi de 21,08%.

Compareceram à votação, no Ceará, 5.905.522 pessoas. Ainda assim, 1.085.522 pessoas que estavam aptas a votar no estado não compareceram ao pleito.

A Justiça Eleitoral reforça que aquele eleitor que não compareceu às urnas no primeiro turno pode votar normalmente no segundo turno . A única condição é que o título de eleitor esteja em situação regular. O documento não é cancelado somente devido à ausência no primeiro turno.

O eleitor pode conferir se o título está regular de duas formas:

Aplicativo e-Título : depois de fazer login, toque em "Mais opções" e, em seguida, "Consultar situação eleitoral".

Site do Autoatendimento Eleitoral : na aba "Consulta", selecione a opção "Situação do título".

Alguns locais de votação foram alterados entre o primeiro e o segundo turno das Eleições 2026 . No Ceará, sete locais tiveram alteração de acordo com a última atualização do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Ceará (TRE-CE).

Houve mudanças em Aracati, Fortaleza, Jardim, Palmácia, Quixadá, Quixeramobim e Santana do Cariri. . Confira na matéria abaixo os locais de votação que mudaram no Ceará:

O TRE-CE informou que as mudanças são pontuais e ocorrem por motivos práticos. A recomendação é que o eleitor confira o local de votação antes de ir votar . A consulta pode ser feita por meio de canais digitais como o aplicativo e-Título, o Autoatendimento Eleitoral e o WhatsApp do TRE-CE - 85 3195.8400.

No estado, o atual presidente teve ampla vantagem e marcou 63,29% dos votos contra 31,27% do candidato do PL, no primeiro turno. Por outro lado, a diferença entre os dois foi de apenas 1,87% na apuração total no país.

Assim, em busca de ampliar o número de eleitores para seus candidatos a presidente, lideranças locais promoveram mobilizações nas redes sociais e nas ruas .

Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula contam com lideranças locais no Ceará para atuar em campanha do 2º turno — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/SVM

Do PT, o governador reeleito do Ceará, Elmano de Freitas, foi um dos responsáveis por liderar a mobilização no estado a favor da reeleição do presidente Lula. O senador Camilo Santana (PT) e o ex-coordenador da campanha de Elmano, Chagas Vieira (PDT), foram recrutados para participarem ativamente da campanha de Lula em todo o Brasil para o segundo turno.

No estado, os senadores eleitos Cid Gomes (PSB) e Luizianne Lins (Rede) também promoveram atos e articulações pró-Lula.

Já no PL, o deputado federal reeleito André Fernandes (PL) - que atingiu a marca em 2026 de mais votado para Câmara dos Deputados da história do Ceará - foi um dos principais articuladores da campanha de Flávio no Ceará. O parlamentar deu continuidade à mobilização do "Bloquinho do 22" após o primeiro turno.

Nomes ligados ao ex-candidato ao governo do Ceará Ciro Gomes (PSDB) anunciaram apoio ao presidenciável do PL, como Roberto Cláudio (União), que foi vice na chapa do tucano . Os outros integrantes da chapa, Capitão Wagner (União) e Alcides Fernandes (PL), também declararam apoio a Flávio.

O próprio Ciro, no entanto, não manifestou publicamente posição sobre o segundo turno da eleição presidencial até o momento.

O Ceará definiu em primeiro turno a eleição para o Governo do Estado: o atual governador, Elmano de Freitas (PT), foi reeleito com 53,19% dos votos válidos . A vice-governadora eleita é Gabriella Aguiar (PSD). Os dois ficam nos cargos pelos próximos quatro anos, de 2027 a 2030.

Para o Senado, foram eleitos os dois candidatos da chapa do governador Elmano de Freitas. Cid Gomes (PSB) e Luizianne Lins (Rede) foram eleitos senadores pelo Ceará com 31,22% e 29,05%, respectivamente. Os mandatos de senadores têm duração de oito anos.

Os eleitores do estado também votaram para redefinir a composição da bancada cearense na Câmara dos Deputados e da Assembleia Legislativa do Ceará (Alece) . Ao todo, os cearenses elegeram 22 deputados federais e 46 deputados estaduais.

articles.title: Por que é fundamental impedir que a diferença seja entendida como menor valor | G1
articles.standfirst: O psiquiatra Bernardo Rahe alerta para o impacto neurológico sofrido pelas minorias vítimas da exposição contínua ao estresse.
articles.summary: O psiquiatra Bernardo Rahe alerta para o impacto neurológico sofrido pelas minorias vítimas da exposição contínua ao estresse.
articles.body:
Hoje é um bom dia para se pensar em diversidade e acolhimento, dois pilares de uma sociedade democrática. Esse foi o pano de fundo da palestra do psiquiatra e psicoterapeuta Bernardo Rahe no Neuro 2026. Com uma trajetória dedicada ao atendimento de pessoas transgênero, ele discorreu sobre como a exposição contínua ao estresse gera impactos neurológicos. “Quando a diferença encontra o preconceito, há uma série de experiências negativas”, afirmou, detalhando como elas se manifestam:

Casal de mulheres: a exposição contínua ao estresse gera impactos neurológicos — Foto: Age without limits

Estigma: associação a estereótipos e à rotulação dos indivíduos.

Discriminação: leva ao tratamento desigual.

Bullying: provoca vitimização recorrente.

Rejeição: o sentimento de pertencimento é apartado, às vezes suprimido.

Barreiras: acesso e participação podem ser dificultados ou até negados.

“Mesmo que o episódio dure apenas alguns minutos, a expectativa de que se repita pode acompanhar a pessoa todos os dias”, explicou. Rahe enfatizou a importância de os pacientes serem ouvidos sobre suas vivências: “A experiência vivida também produz informação científica, e escutar não significa abandonar o método científico”.

O psiquiatra apresentou as consequências do estresse relacionado ao preconceito e como ele interfere na saúde mental:

Estressores distais (externos): discriminação, rejeição, violência bullying e barreiras institucionais.

Processos proximais (internos e relacionais): expectativa de rejeição, estigma internalizado, ocultação da identidade, hipervigilância.

Desfechos associados: ansiedade e depressão, isolamento, exaustão, menor procura por ajuda.

Masking (camuflagem): há um custo invisível por trás das tentativas de garantir segurança e aceitação. “Nesse caso, o que ‘aparece’ é uma boa adaptação, ou alta funcionalidade, mas o que pode estar camuflado é o esforço constante e a exaustão, além da ausência de suporte”, ressaltou.

Rahe chamou a atenção para o fato de que, na população em geral, a prevalência estimada do Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) gira em torno de 1% a 2%. No entanto, entre pessoas atendidas por disforia ou incongruência de gênero, esse percentual é de 11%. Novamente, contextualizou como a diversidade enfrenta o preconceito:

Pessoas neurodivergentes: sofrem com barreiras sensoriais, regras implícitas, comunicação não adaptada e infantilização.

População LGBTQIA+: lida com a rejeição e a invalidação identitária em um sistema que impõe a cisheteronormatividade – isto é, a cisgeneridade (quando o indivíduo se identifica com o gênero atribuído ao nascer) e a heterossexualidade como as únicas formas naturais e legítimas de existência.

“Há uma via de risco que inclui discriminação, estigma internalizado, masking, hipervigilância, exaustão, isolamento, ansiedade e depressão. E uma via de proteção, com escuta, identidade positiva, adaptações, acessibilidade, autonomia, bem-estar e participação. A verdadeira superação não é parecer menos diferente, é impedir que a diferença seja convertida em menor valor”, finalizou.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: 6 milhões de eleitores devem votar no 2º turno no Pará  | G1
articles.standfirst: Eleitores que não votaram no primeiro turno podem ir às urnas no próximo domingo, mesmo sem ter justificado ausência. Aviões, helicópteros, barcos e até tração animal foram usados para distribuir urnas.
articles.summary: Eleitores que não votaram no primeiro turno podem ir às urnas no próximo domingo, mesmo sem ter justificado ausência. Aviões, helicópteros, barcos e até tração animal foram usados
articles.body:
Neste domingo (25), 6,2 milhões de eleitores do Pará devem ir às urnas no segundo turno das Eleições 2026 para escolher o presidente da República. As seções eleitorais funcionam das 8h às 17h em todo estado, mesmo horário de Brasília. Para votar, o eleitor deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto aos mesários.

No primeiro turno, mais de 1 milhão de eleitores não foram às urnas no estado paraense. Os 5.062.269 que compareceram, escolheram governador , os dois senadores e deputados estaduais e federais .

Mas mesmo os eleitores que não compareceram às urnas podem ir votar no segundo turno, mesmo sem ter justificado ausência.

🗳️ Em todo Pará são 22.072 seções eleitorais. Os eleitores precisam ficar atentos, pois houve mudanças em alguns locais de votação. A orientação é verificar antes de ir votar se seu local de votação está entre os que tiveram mudanças.

Para garantir a participação dos cidadãos no segundo turno, o TRE do Pará informou que montou um plano logístico para enfrentar a seca no estado, que afeta rios e o transporte de eleitores. Algumas comunidades indígenas enfrentaram dificuldades para votar no primeiro turno e a Justiça determinou que a União providencie medidas.

Aviões, helicópteros e até tração animal

Aviões auxiliam na distribuição de urnas em Altamira, no Pará — Foto: Reprodução / TV Liberal

📦 Para distribuir as urnas em todo o Pará, o TRE mobilizará 5.998 veículos, divididos da seguinte forma:

4.786 veículos terrestres, para transporte por estradas e vias urbanas;

1.203 embarcações, para atender localidades com acesso pelos rios;

9 veículos aéreos, para o transporte de equipamentos por via aérea.

Por conta da estiagem no Pará, principalmente no Oeste e Sudoeste, rios estão com volume de água mais baixo, o que afeta o deslocamento de embarcações. Com isso, barcos menores devem ser usados, segundo o TRE, e até tração animal.

“Em regiões como o Marajó e o Baixo Amazonas, onde o nível dos rios caiu severamente e surgiram bancos de areia, a navegação de médio e grande porte foi inviabilizada. Nesses locais, o transporte fluvial será feito por barcos de menor calado. Já onde os rios secaram completamente, as urnas eletrônicas e as equipes técnicas chegarão por transporte terrestre alternativo, incluindo tração animal e esforço humano”, informou o TRE.

A operação logística do TRE para distribuir as urnas levou em consideração também as características geográficas do Pará, que possui comunidades rurais, ribeirinhas e localidades de difícil acesso. O TRE não detalhou o quantitativo de veículos de tração animal que podem ser usados.

A estrutura inclui levar urnas a locais de votação em áreas de diferentes características, além das seções em áreas urbanas:

articles.summary: Resultado oficial consolidado da eleição só será divulgado após as 17h (horário de Brasília).
articles.body:
O candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) venceu o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) na China , segundo boletins de urna disponibilizados pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) neste domingo (25), dia do segundo turno das eleições 2026.

Lula recebeu 502 votos (65,28%), enquanto Flávio teve 267 votos (34,72%), segundo boletins de urna divulgados pelo TSE até o momento.

Os dois candidatos ampliaram suas votações em relação ao primeiro turno. Na ocasião, Lula recebeu 367 votos, contra 203 de Flávio Bolsonaro.

O resultado mantém a vantagem do petista registrada no país em 2022. Naquele ano, Lula venceu Jair Bolsonaro no segundo turno na China, com 279 votos (53,65%), contra 241 (46,35%) do então presidente.

Ao todo, quase 1 milhão de brasileiros que vivem no exterior estão aptos a votar neste segundo turno. A votação ocorre em 186 cidades de mais de cem países. (Acompanhe aqui os resultados por país).

Ao longo deste domingo, o g1 realiza um levantamento dos boletins de urna divulgados pelo TSE em diferentes partes do mundo , para antecipar os números da apuração no exterior.

O resultado consolidado da eleição, no entanto, só será divulgado pelo TSE após as 17h (horário de Brasília), quando termina a votação no Brasil.

Veja países em que Lula ou Flávio Bolsonaro venceram até agora. — Foto: Arte/g1

O número representa um aumento de 31,8% em relação a 2022, e o maior contingente desde 1989. No entanto, o percentual de comparecimento é menor que o registrado nas duas eleições presidenciais anteriores.

Em 2022, 301.509 eleitores votaram no exterior no primeiro turno, o equivalente a 43,83% dos aptos. Naquele ano, Lula também foi o candidato mais votado pelos brasileiros no exterior, com 47,17% dos votos.

Os brasileiros com domicílio eleitoral no exterior votam apenas para presidente e vice-presidente da República. Para participar da eleição fora do país, é necessário ter transferido previamente o domicílio eleitoral para uma zona eleitoral no exterior.

articles.title: Serbia votes in election pitting longtime leader against student movement
articles.summary: Polls show populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in a tight race against the anticorruption and antirepression movement.
articles.body:
Serbians have begun voting in parliamentary elections amid a mass student protest ⁠movement that seeks to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has held power as prime minister and then president for more than a decade.

Sunday’s snap elections, called by Vucic in September, follow almost two years of student-led demonstrations that have accused the government of corruption ⁠and ruling for those in power rather than the people. The movement was triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024.

The students have since gained widespread support.

A loss for Vucic ⁠would mark a profound political shift in the Balkan country of six million people and would be reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary’s Viktor Orban in April.

But Vucic, who resigned as president in September to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia out of economic obscurity and ‌orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation.

During the campaign, Vucic has promised higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare and subsidies for young couples. He has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union.

But relations with the EU have frayed under his leadership. The bloc has grown increasingly frustrated over a lack of reforms addressing the judiciary, the rule of law and corruption.

The Student List movement’s agenda focuses on rooting out corruption and improving education while saying little about its international ambitions.

Its roster of 250 largely unfamiliar candidates, including university professors, actors and farmers, is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic.

Its campaign is more about ending graft, restoring the rule of law and rebuilding institutions than issues such as Russia, EU membership or normalising relations with Kosovo, which declared independence from Serbia in 2008, said Jelena Vasiljevic, a senior research associate at the University of Belgrade’s Institute for Philosophy and Social Theory.

“The political dynamic has changed from the ground up,” she told Al Jazeera.

Young people, long considered the country’s most politically disengaged group, have become the core of its largest social mobilisation in decades, she said.

Turnout will be decisive, Vasiljevic said.

Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) retains a disciplined core electorate, supported by a clientelist model of government in which goods and services are exchanged for political support, she said. The Student List must not only unite opposition-minded voters but also mobilise habitual nonvoters and the undecided.

Opinion polls are predicting a tight race.

An Ipsos poll published on Thursday suggested the SNS would win 47 percent ⁠of the vote to the students’ 40 percent although other polls have put the students ahead.

Rights groups and activists said repression has worsened since the train station canopy collapse, which was widely blamed on government corruption.

About 150,000 supporters of the student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday.

Vucic and his party have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents.

The former president claims the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students deny.

Polling stations opened at 7am (06:00 GMT) and close at 8pm (19:00 GMT) with first indications of results expected about two hours later.

articles.title: In 1906, a gold discovery attracted 700 people to Skidoo, California, turning it into a $1.5 million mining hub before the boom ended and residents left just after a decade
articles.summary: A gold discovery in 1906 transformed a remote part of California's Death Valley region into a busy mining settlement.
articles.body: A gold discovery in 1906 transformed a remote part of California's Death Valley region into a busy mining settlement. Skidoo attracted hundreds of people hoping to make their fortunes, eventually growing to a population of around 700. The town became one of the area's most important gold-mining centres, producing approximately $1.5 million in revenue during its main period of activity. However, the settlement's success depended on difficult mining conditions and the ability to transport water across the desert. As mining activity declined, residents gradually left, turning Skidoo into a ghost town.Skidoo attracted 700 people after the 1906 gold discoveryAccording to the US National Park Service, two prospectors discovered gold in the area in 1906. Their find attracted interest in a region where mining offered the possibility of substantial financial rewards, despite the challenges of working in a remote desert environment.Skidoo developed in the Panamint Mountains within what is now Death Valley National Park. Its growth formed part of a wider period of renewed interest in gold and silver mining across the Death Valley region during the early 20th century.Skidoo was the region's largest mining operation between 1907 and 1917. The settlement reached a population of approximately 700, with people arriving to work in the mines and support the growing community.Western Mining History also reports that Skidoo had a newspaper, a bank, a school and telephone service at its height in 1907. These facilities reflected how quickly a remote mining camp developed into a functioning town.The settlement's growth was not simply a result of the gold discovery. Extracting the metal required infrastructure, workers and a reliable supply of water, all of which had to be established in a challenging landscape.A long pipeline helped the mining operation growOne of Skidoo's biggest challenges was obtaining enough water to process the gold-bearing rock. The town's location in an arid region made a dependable supply essential to its mining activities.The National Park Service states that a 23-mile metal pipeline was constructed to carry water to the mill and the town. The system connected the mining operation with a distant water source, allowing the processing facility to operate in an otherwise dry environment.Western Mining History describes the pipeline as an important undertaking associated with mine owner Bob Montgomery. Water was carried from Birch Spring, high on the western side of Telescope Peak, to the mill. The pipeline provided water to prospectors exploring isolated parts of the desert.Building such a system required considerable investment and planning. Without a steady water supply, the operation would have struggled to process ore on a large scale. The pipeline therefore became a crucial part of Skidoo's development, supporting both gold extraction and activity in the surrounding area.The mill opened in 1907, according to the National Park Service. Its purpose was to extract gold from the ore brought from the mines. The construction of the facility marked an important step in turning the original discovery into a more organised mining enterprise.How much gold revenue did Skidoo produceSkidoo became one of California's notable gold-mining settlements during its relatively short period of prosperity. The NPS estimates that the operation generated about $1.5 million in revenue during its main mining years.The figure illustrates the scale of the operation, although it represents historical revenue rather than the town's value in modern money. It also shows that Skidoo's success rested on more than a single discovery, with numerous mining claims contributing to the area's output.Production continued as miners worked to extract gold from the surrounding deposits. In September 1908, the Los Angeles Herald reported that gold bricks worth $10,000 from the Skidoo mines had arrived in nearby Rhyolite before being sent to the mint. The shipment represented 15 days of production and was considered typical of the preceding 3 months.The ore was also increasing in both quantity and quality at the time. However, the revenue figures alone do not capture the practical difficulties of operating in the desert.Skidoo's prosperity faded after 1917The mining boom eventually lost momentum. According to the NPS, Skidoo was the Death Valley region's largest mining operation from 1907 to 1917, but most residents moved away after 1917.The decline reflected the uncertain nature of mining settlements, whose fortunes depended heavily on the continued viability of local mineral deposits. Once the main period of activity ended, the town could no longer sustain the population and services that had developed around the mines.Mining did not stop completely when residents began leaving. Sporadic milling continued until 1942, when Skidoo was completely abandoned. Western Mining History notes that mining took place in the district again during the 1930s, demonstrating that interest in its gold deposits persisted even after the original town had largely disappeared.Nevertheless, these later efforts did not restore Skidoo to its earlier prominence.The surviving mill preserves Skidoo's mining historyToday, Skidoo forms part of the historic mining landscape within Death Valley National Park. Although the town itself has largely disappeared, remnants of its industrial past remain visible.NPS identifies the Skidoo Historic District as a site listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Its surviving features include tanks, mercury tables and substantial portions of the mill operations. The structure provides evidence of the equipment and infrastructure required to extract gold in the early 20th century.The site also illustrates the lasting environmental challenges associated with historical mining. articles.title: In 2017, Alaska laid steel-fiber rubber concrete panels on Abbott Road; field tests found less rutting than nearby asphalt, while laboratory tests indicated freeze-thaw resistance
articles.summary: Discover how Alaska's steel-fiber rubber concrete panels are outperforming traditional asphalt in durability and freeze-thaw resistance, offering a solution to cold weather road problems.
articles.body: Anyone who has driven through a cold northern city at the end of winter knows how quickly a road surface can lose its shape. Wear comes from studded tires, meltwater that seeps into cracks and refreezes overnight and heavy vehicles repeatedly traveling the same wheel paths at intersections. Rutting, the formation of grooves known as ruts in the wheel paths, is a typical problem of asphalt under repeated loads.This issue has always been present in Anchorage and local engineers have been studying for a long time what surface material could withstand the stress at the intersection point and other high-traffic areas. While concrete does not change its shape, it is known for cracking due to changing temperatures. Rubber, used together with concrete, makes it more elastic, but decreases some of its mechanical properties. To compensate for it, the Alaskan researchers introduced short steel fibers. Such material was studied in the laboratory and on the real road and the results of both experiments are presented in this paper.Laboratory and cast-in-place results that preceded the road testThe first study, Use of Steel Fiber-Reinforced Rubberized Concrete in Cold Regions, appears in the U.S. Department of Transportation’s ROSAP repository with a December 24, 2017 date and it describes the research as beginning with laboratory wheel tracker and freeze-thaw testing, followed by a small experimental cast-in-place panel trial. The abstract reports that wheel tracker tests showed much lower rutting for SFRRC than for asphalt and that freeze-thaw testing showed less cracking and strength reduction than for Portland cement concrete. The team ran these laboratory tests at the University of Alaska Anchorage, where an experimental cast-in-place panel then showed little wear under traffic, a result that informed the design of the pre-cast panels for Abbott Road.Precast panel installation on Abbott Road in summer 2017The precast panels for the Abbott Road project were designed, built and installed in summer 2017. The ROSAP study says the Abbott Road installation was meant to test at full scale, on a high-traffic urban arterial road, what the laboratory and campus results had suggested about rutting, freeze-thaw durability, construction process and life cycle cost. The study also says the panels would be monitored to determine whether SFRRC could be used on roadways.Phase II field comparison with hot mix asphalt on the adjacent sectionThe research section of the Alaska Department of Transportation & Public Facilities website hosts this second report, which contains the practical field evaluation of the SFRRC. The Phase II report compared the SFRRC sections with adjoining hot mix asphalt sections. The main findings of the summary were that SFRRC road surfaces had considerable rutting resistance when compared to the adjoining asphalt samples. The freeze-thaw results were stated in the same part, which was also tested against the lab results from the earlier cited test.Planned monitoring from 2017 to 2020 and use at intersectionsThe December 2017 study covers the laboratory and cast-in-place work and the Abbott Road plan; the Phase II report documents the field comparison findings; and the broader program, scheduled to run through December 31, 2020, was set out separately. A project listing at the National Concrete Pavement Technology Center describes an experimental feature evaluation of the SFRRC installed on Abbott Road, sponsored by the Federal Highway Administration and led by researcher Carolyn Morehouse. This listing has a start date of January 1, 2017 and an end date of December 31, 2020. In addition, it states that data will be collected for three years following construction for material wear, operation and pavement conditions, with comparisons from control sites.After this period, a synopsis was to be prepared that would include recommendations on the use of SFRRC in Alaska and it might also address issues that better specification and construction and maintenance practices could have prevented. Phase II evaluated SFRRC on a public road and the research recommended its further use at highway intersections and in test sections on major arterial roads, as described in the 2023 study published in the Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bots, deepfakes and surveillance: Israel’s election goes to war online
articles.summary: Netanyahu and his rivals are tied days from the vote, and both camps are fighting with bots, deepfakes and data.
articles.body:
Polls show the blocs linked to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the opposition, led by former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, are locked in a virtual tie before Tuesday’s general election.

Efforts to mobilise supporters, win voters and attack opponents are being played out online through a series of social media advertisements and doctored AI videos. Many of these paint a bleak vision, the outcome depending on whether the party is on the right or centre, of Israel if their rivals win.

On Thursday, the Israeli liberal daily Haaretz reported that dozens of online bots created to undermine the Iranian government were being repurposed to spread campaign propaganda supporting Netanyahu and his Likud party, and warn voters of the dangers posed by Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who make up part of the opposition bloc .

Both camps are pushing AI-generated and deepfake videos on X. Several of them show Netanyahu confronting his alleged failings before the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023; others show the opposition being sympathetic to Arab parties (those representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel) which have been perceived by many as kingmakers in the coming election.

“We’re competing against parties with far greater budgets and technological resources, particularly the Likud,” Mauricio Lapchik, director of the Arab-dominated Joint List Hebrew-language campaign, said. “The use of technology is clearly deepening an already unequal playing field … We may not have the same resources, but we are convinced that our message matters more than the artificial technology behind it.”

Significant resources have been used by the Israeli right against the left-wing Joint List – an alliance of Hadash, Balad and Ta’al – and Ra’am, also known as the United Arab List. Palestinian citizens of Israel generally support one of these two blocs, and all the parties have faced legal challenges before the parliamentary election .

Likud were looking to use Elector, an app that tracks voter turnout on election day, but were restricted by the Central Elections Committee due to privacy concerns. They will instead use a new app named Victory 26 . Unlike Elector, this does not reveal the identities of voters but would allow Likud activists and officials to determine which areas have the lowest turnout, manually take the names of people who have cast their votes, and then target those who have not yet.

Likud is encouraging supporters and potential sympathisers to download and use the app on election day, according to Haaretz.

This app could play a crucial role in the election, which will likely be determined by voter turnout.

“Elector and similar programmes are very basic compared to what the Israeli military is capable of now,” Sebastian Ben Daniel, a doctoral researcher into algorithms, computability, and AI, said. “Israel has the perfect laboratory with which to develop this kind of technology.”

Privacy issues are a particular concern for the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population and whose political activity is already heavily monitored.

In recent weeks, Finance Minister Belazel Smotrich caused uproar when he released an AI video showing the Supreme Court’s president, a justice and the attorney general – all frequent targets of the far-right government who have sought to shake off judicial oversight – being violently dragged from an antigovernment protest.

In another AI video shared by Netanyahu earlier this year, his key political rival Eisenkot is seen running towards an AI figure who many believe resembled his son, Gal, who was killed while taking part in the genocide on Gaza, before passing him entirely and embracing the head of the Arab Ra’am party, Mansour Abbas.

Netanyahu’s camp later said they did not intend the figure to mirror Eisenkot’s son, who wears a T-shirt saying “Israel’s Unity” in Hebrew, and replaced the male character with a female one.

There has also been heavy use of AI to demonise Palestinian citizens of Israel, with a video shared by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir portraying the people of Gaza as donkeys, and “herding” them to Paris. Ben-Gvir has called for the ethnic cleansing of Gaza via “voluntary emigration” and frequently targets Palestinians in his political stunts, such as humiliating detainees and prisoners in Israeli jails .

There has also been a heavy use of bots by Netanyahu and Ben-Gvir’s campaign to amplify their political messaging, according to numerous accounts.

“The online campaign has been especially violent. AI, algorithms and data management are all utilised to cement what we call ‘affective polarisation’,” Roi Zur a lecturer at Essex University and specialist in voting behaviour and election strategies, told Al Jazeera. This term is used by political scientists to refer to the entrenchment of political blocs and an increased animosity towards the opposing side.

“Affective polarisation targets people at the fringe, who might be thinking of voting for a party in an opposing bloc, and bring them back into the fold.” As this election will likely be determined by the success of the smaller parties and voter turnout in general, this is a pertinent point.

“Turnout and management of the parties will be essential. If you look at large secular cities, such as Tel Aviv or Haifa, turnout is typically only 60 percent,” he said. “If you compare that to cities and towns with a large Haredi (ultra -Orthodox) population, such as Jerusalem and Bnei Brak, the turnout is around 80 to 85 percent, so a large part of the campaigning is also to get people out to vote by threatening them with the ‘other’.”

An Israeli soldier stands under a surveillance camera at a checkpoint in the flashpoint Palestinian city of Hebron. Israel’s army has deployed a sweeping personal data collection programme using facial recognition technology against Palestinians in parts of the occupied West Bank [File: Hazem Bader/AFP]

articles.title: 12 injured, including several minors, in shooting near Florida A&M University stadium
articles.summary: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.
articles.body: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday. The Tallahassee Police Department said in a statement that 11 of the 12 were shot and that three victims had serious injuries, with one minor in serious condition. The others, it said, were in stable condition. Six of the injured are under 18 years old and the youngest is 11 years old, Chief Lawrence Revell of the Tallahassee Police Department said at a press conference early Sunday morning. “Our preliminary information shows that an altercation occurred between individuals,” he added, describing it as “an isolated incident between two or three individuals.” Revell said that no arrests had yet been made, nor anyone taken into custody, but that police believed one shooter was involved. “Our priority is to determine what happened and why it happened, and to bring the people that are responsible for this to justice,” he added, asking any witnesses to come forward. The violence unfolded about 8 p.m. at an intersection adjacent to Bragg Memorial Stadium, it said. Early in the evening, Florida A&M’s Rattlers hosted the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions for the historically Black university’s annual homecoming game. After the shooting took place, the university issued a statement on X asking members of its campus community to stay away from the area. It described the shooting as having taken place “near campus,” which it said was safe. “Our hearts are with the victims and everyone affected by tonight’s incident on Perry Street,” the university said. Florida State University, about a mile away from Florida A&M, issued an emergency alert about the violence and said it didn’t appear anyone from its school community was involved. “As a precaution, students, faculty and staff in the Tallahassee area are advised to remain indoors this evening and stay alert,” it said. Revell offered condolences to the victims and their families, and also praised officers who he said ran without hesitation “into the middle of this, still not knowing where the shooters were, still not knowing how many victims we had.” “We had officers that were picking up victims and carrying them in their arms to transport victims because they couldn’t get through the mass of people,” he said. The investigation into the violence was ongoing, and police asked witnesses to come forward.

articles.title: Nigeria’s missing: Families in the northeast still wait for answers
articles.summary: People across northeastern Nigeria continue searching for loved ones who went missing during years of violence.
articles.body:
Maiduguri, Nigeria – For more than 15 years, Kashim Mohammed has hoped that his younger sister, Falmata Mohammed, is still alive.

Falmata disappeared in 2011 while travelling with her mother from Maiduguri, the capital of northeastern Nigeria’s Borno State, to Port Harcourt in the south. According to Kashim, the two women were abducted by unidentified gunmen.

Years later, a man approached Kashim at Baga Road Market in Maiduguri with news that briefly revived the family’s hopes of finding the women. He claimed Falmata had been found in Benin and was searching for her relatives.

But the man disappeared without leaving contact details. Kashim said he has never been able to establish whether the information was genuine.

“From then until now, nobody knows anything about the man who brought the information,” he said.

Kashim, 39, chairs the Association for the Well-being of Displaced and Missing Persons’ Families, a community organisation based in Bolori II, Ngarnam ward, Maiduguri. He said years of violence have torn his family apart.

“As a result of the violence, I lost my sister from the same father,” he said.

Their father, Mohammed Kolo, worked at Maiduguri’s State Specialist Hospital. Kashim said his father died at 60 from an illness he attributed to high blood pressure without learning what had happened to his daughter.

Kolo had refused to abandon hope that she would return.

“Our father always said, ‘Wherever she is, I believe my daughter is alive,’” Kashim recalled.

For Muhammad Alhaji Bashir, the disappearance of his elder brother, Adam Muhammad Bashir, known as Bakura, has left a similar void.

Muhammad, 29, said Bakura went missing around 2012 or 2013 when Muhammad was about 14. His brother, then believed to be in his early 20s, sold cosmetics in a Maiduguri market and was studying civil engineering at Ramat Polytechnic, according to Muhammad.

“I sincerely lost my brother as a result of the Boko Haram crisis,” Muhammad said.

Boko Haram’s armed rebellion began in northeastern Nigeria in 2009. The conflict has devastated communities through attacks, abductions and displacement, leaving families searching for relatives whose fates remain unknown.

Muhammad said Bakura’s family searched across Maiduguri. A rehabilitation centre offered them some hope.

“Whenever we heard that rescued people had been brought to the rehabilitation centre in Bulumkutu, we went there with Bakura’s pictures, but unfortunately, nobody recognised him,” Muhammad said.

Muhammad said his father and stepmother, who was Bakura’s mother, later died from illnesses the family attributed to hypertension. He and other relatives continue to search, without confirmation of whether Bakura is alive or dead.

Thousands of families, thousands of questions

The two families’ experiences reflect the uncertainty facing relatives of people who have disappeared during more than a decade of conflict in northeastern Nigeria.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), working with the Nigerian Red Cross Society, has supported efforts to trace missing people and reconnect separated families.

Local advocates for missing people cited an estimate of 17,000 people missing across northern Nigeria, many of them linked to the conflict involving Boko Haram and its aftermath. Kashim said his association’s records indicated that about 10,000 people are missing in Borno State alone. He added that many families have yet to register their missing relatives.

The sources for the estimates cited by advocates and the association, their geographical coverage, reporting periods and methods of compilation have not been independently established for this article.

Behind the estimates are families who have spent years searching, parents who have died without learning what happened to their children and children growing up without a parent.

Some people reportedly disappeared during attacks on their communities. Others became separated from relatives while fleeing violence or travelling between towns. Families search hospitals, displacement camps and centres receiving people rescued from conflict areas, often following leads that prove impossible to verify.

Even when names, photographs and personal details are submitted to organisations involved in tracing missing people, locating relatives can take time.

Kashim said his search for Falmata helped motivate him and other affected families to establish their association in 2023. He said the organisation obtained registration with Nigeria’s Corporate Affairs Commission in 2025.

Members meet monthly to share information and discuss their circumstances. Some families have reported losing eight or nine relatives, according to Kashim.

“In our community of Bolori II, we have many families who lost their relatives as a result of years of violence that ravaged northeastern Nigeria,” he said.

Kashim said the group sometimes receives notices from the Red Cross containing names and details of missing people. These can give families leads to pursue although they do not necessarily mean a relative has been located.

The association also supports children affected by the disappearances. Kashim said it was assisting about 600 orphaned children from affected families. Some attend school while others have dropped out because their relatives cannot afford to pay for their education or other basic needs.

“We are now suffering because of the harsh living conditions,” he said, adding that the ICRC had distributed relief items to some families.

When a missing person is a parent or breadwinner, relatives must cope with lost income while trying to provide food, shelter and schooling for children. The association’s work has consequently expanded beyond tracing missing people to helping families manage the hardships their disappearances leave behind.

The search became harder for some families after devastating floods struck parts of Maiduguri in 2024.

Kashim said floodwaters submerged parts of Ngarnam and destroyed photographs that families had kept to help identify missing relatives.

Photographs can be vital when families try to identify people who have been rescued, displaced or found in unfamiliar communities. Without them, relatives must rely on names, physical descriptions and memories.

Kashim said some families now have little beyond remembered details and surviving records to help identify their relatives.

The floods added another obstacle to searches already complicated by years of conflict, displacement and uncertainty.

For Kashim, finding Falmata would resolve a question that has haunted his family since 2011. His father died believing she might still return, and the family has never established whether the report of her discovery in Benin was true.

Muhammad’s search for Bakura continues without the parents who once helped him look for his brother.

Both families are appealing to anyone who may have information about their missing relatives. For them, finding an answer would mean more than ending a search: It would establish what happened to someone whose absence has shaped their lives for years.

Kashim’s message to his sister remains a plea for a reunion that his family has waited years to see.

“Falmata Mohammed, if you are alive anywhere in this world, we are the family of late Mohammed Kolo in Bolori II, Ngarnam. We are waiting for you,” he said.

articles.title: Florida A&M University shooting leaves 12 injured, including 6 children, near football stadium
articles.summary: A shooting near Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium left 12 people injured, including six juveniles, the youngest just 11 years old.
articles.body: At least 12 people, including six juveniles, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee on Saturday night, authorities said. The Tallahassee Police Department said the shooting occurred just before 8 p.m. near the intersection of Perry and Manatee streets, close to Bragg Memorial Stadium. Authorities said 12 people were injured, including 11 who sustained gunshot wounds. One victim was in critical condition, two others were seriously injured and eight were listed in stable condition, police said. SEVERAL UNIVERSITY OF IOWA STUDENTS WOUNDED IN DOWNTOWN SHOOTING AFTER FIGHT ERUPTS NEAR CAMPUS Of the 12 known victims, six are adults and six are juveniles, Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence E. Revell said during a news conference. The youngest victim was 11 years old, according to Revell. "Tonight, our thoughts are with the victims and their families as they face the devastating impact of this violence," Revell said. "It is especially heartbreaking to know that children are among those injured," he continued. "In the moments immediately following the shooting, and before the scene was fully secure, our officers put their own safety at risk to carry victims to safety and transport them to the hospital. Their actions were nothing short of heroic and reflect the courage and compassion our officers bring to this community every day." BOY, 12, KILLED AFTER SUSPECT OPENED FIRE DURING BRAWL NEAR THEATER DISTRICT, POLICE SAY Police said preliminary information indicated a physical altercation occurred before the shooting. Authorities described the altercation as an isolated incident involving two or three individuals. No arrests had been announced as of the latest police update. The shooting occurred during Florida A&M University's Homecoming Week, as students and alumni gathered in Tallahassee for the annual celebrations. Florida A&M University said the incident occurred near campus. The university said the campus remained safe and urged people to avoid the area. "Our hearts go out to the victims and all those affected by this tragic incident," the university said. "While the campus remains safe, individuals are encouraged to avoid the area to allow law enforcement to conduct its investigation." Tallahassee Mayor John Dailey expressed condolences following the shooting. "This is a truly horrific and heartbreaking tragedy," Dailey posted on X. "Tonight and in the days ahead, the FAMU family is not alone. Our entire community stands with you." The Tallahassee Police Department's Violent Crimes Unit is investigating the shooting as detectives work to identify those responsible.
