articles.title: Were they beheaded? Did they get lawyers? Bangladesh seeks answers from Saudi Arabia over execution of 'couple'
articles.summary: Bangladesh has sought detailed information from Saudi Arabia about the execution of two of its citizens in the Makkah region, including the charges
articles.body: Bangladesh has sought detailed information from Saudi Arabia about the execution of two of its citizens in the Makkah region, including the charges against them, court verdicts, method of execution and whether they had legal representation during their trials, according to a media report.The Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah sent a diplomatic letter to the Saudi ministry of foreign affairs' branch in Makkah on October 19, seeking answers to six questions, Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo reported on Sunday.Bangladesh's consul general in Jeddah also raised the matter with a senior Saudi foreign ministry official during a meeting on the same day, the report said.The two Bangladeshi nationals, a man and a woman, were executed on October 14 after being convicted of committing an “indecent act” inside a mosque in Makkah.Dhaka seeks details of charges, trials and executionsIn its diplomatic communication, Bangladesh sought details of the offences for which the two citizens were convicted, including when and where the alleged acts took place. It also requested their arrest dates and certified copies of the court verdicts, Prothom Alo reported.Dhaka has asked Saudi authorities whether the death sentences were carried out by beheading or another method. It has also sought information about the whereabouts of the bodies and whether they would be repatriated to Bangladesh or had already been buried in Saudi Arabia.The letter further asks whether lawyers represented the two citizens during the investigation and trial, and whether they had sought legal assistance.Bangladeshi officials said the country's diplomatic missions did not have detailed information about the legal proceedings leading to the executions, including whether the two individuals had been represented by lawyers.Saudi authorities had not responded to the consulate's latest diplomatic communication, the newspaper reported, citing Bangladeshi officials.Discrepancy over charges and sentencesDhaka is also seeking clarification over information contained in a list of Bangladeshi prisoners shared by Saudi authorities in September.The list reportedly included allegations of adultery and an information technology-related offence involving the two citizens. However, it did not specify their sentences.Bangladesh is seeking an explanation for the discrepancy between those entries and the Saudi interior ministry's public explanation of the executions.The Bangladeshi government had also raised the matter with the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka, according to the Dhaka Tribune.Bangladeshi officials said the government had not received detailed official information from Saudi authorities before learning that the executions had taken place, the newspaper reported last week.Dhaka has also sought details about 20 other Bangladeshi citizens whose names appeared on the Saudi prisoner list as convicted, but whose sentences were not specified.The latest diplomatic communication comes as Bangladesh seeks further information about the circumstances surrounding the October 14 executions and the legal proceedings against the two citizens.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chelsea's World's End Estate to get £20m refurbishment
articles.summary: The council plans to improve 750 homes, in seven tower blocks, including new kitchens and bathrooms.
articles.body:
Chelsea's World's End Estate has been earmarked for £20m worth of refurbishment.

Kensington and Chelsea Council has proposed a scheme of work for the 750 homes in west London, set across seven tower blocks, which includes replacing some of the kitchens and bathrooms, roof renewals and redecoration of communal areas.

Leaseholders will have to contribute towards the repairs, although the amount has not yet been confirmed.

There will be tailored support for residents most affected by the works, including respite and the option to temporarily live away.

The work to the interior of the flats, as well as the roofs and communal areas, is estimated to cost around £16.5m, and would be due to start in March 2028 and be completed one year later.

The refurbishment would also include a £3.8m lift renewal programme estimated to start in February 2028.

Over £500,000 has also been earmarked for proposed electrical and fire safety improvements.

The heat network on the estate will also be upgraded, to ensure it is in compliance with new Ofgem regulations.

These require everyone on a heat network to be billed individually for the energy they use.

A report to the council's Housing and Communities Select Committee said that although there is building metering across World's End, "the age and condition of the existing system" means that it cannot currently support individual heat billing.

"It will not be easy to upgrade the system at World's End, and is estimated to require significant investment," the report says.

"This is an area of concern for many leaseholders, as the work needed would generate significant leaseholder recharges."

The report adds: "The World's End Estate programme represents a major long-term investment in the estate's fabric, safety and infrastructure.

"With over £20m of planned investment, extensive resident engagement already undertaken, and clear delivery plans in place, the programme offers a significant opportunity to improve homes, enhance resident safety and secure the future of the estate for decades to come."

articles.title: Qatar official calls for peace and security to boost trade, investment
articles.summary: The Qatari minister of state for trade says peace and security are essential for prosperity in trade and investment.
articles.body:
Doha, Qatar – Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Trade Affairs Ahmad bin Mohammed al-Sayed has called for greater international cooperation and economic stability, warning that trade and investment cannot flourish without peace and security.

Speaking at the United Nations-led World Investment Forum in Doha on Sunday, al-Sayed said geopolitical upheaval and growing economic fragmentation were threatening global investment prospects.

“The global economy is undergoing changes. There are geopolitical changes. These are all issues that redefine the landscape of global investment,” he said.

“We believe that investment in the future is related to investment in peace and security,” the minister added.

“Trade will prosper, and long-term investment will create its potential only with a safe and stable environment.”

Organised by the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), the World Investment Forum brings together heads of state, policymakers, CEOs and investors to discuss global investment, opportunities, challenges and sustainable development.

Al-Sayed’s remarks come as several conflicts continue to rage around the world, and with growing fears of an escalation in the US-Israel war on Iran in the coming weeks.

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments, has been disrupted since the US and Israel launched the war on February 28. Iran responded by effectively blocking the strait and attacking targets across the region.

Prior to the war, one-fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas flowed through the strait.

In the past week, escalating attacks on shipping in the strait and uncertainty over diplomatic efforts to end the nearly eight-month war have led to a surge in oil prices, putting further pressure on the global economy.

On Thursday, oil prices climbed about 4 percent to a five-month high, with Brent futures crossing $113.17 a barrel.

Al-Sayed stressed the need for predictable international rules and stronger economic partnerships at a time of heightened uncertainty.

“In our world, which is facing further uncertainty and economic fragmentation, our message stays clear. It is a call for further cooperation and less isolation, further cooperation and less division,” he said.

Iranian strikes on Qatar’s Ras Laffan industrial complex in March damaged facilities, with repairs expected to take several years.

The minister outlined Qatar’s efforts to strengthen supply chains, diversify economic partnerships and “open new markets for our exports”.

He said Qatar attracted 373 foreign direct investment projects in 2025, a 50 percent increase from the previous year, generating more than 15,000 jobs.

Qatar has also unveiled infrastructure projects worth $38.5bn over the next five years, alongside an anticipated $22.5bn in private sector investment in hospitality and real estate, al-Sayed added.

articles.title: Former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot emerges as Netanyahu’s leading election challenger
articles.summary: A decorated former Israeli army chief has emerged as a leading election challenger after serving in the war cabinet and suffering devastating personal losses following the Oct. 7 attacks.
articles.body: JERUSALEM — Israel’s high-stakes election on Oct. 27 pits the longest serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, against the highly decorated retired Lt. Gen. Gadi Eisenkot. While fairly new to politics, Eisenkot has an impressive resume that could help him become the Jewish state's next leader. According to a number of polls, Eisenkot's centrist political party, Yashar, has a narrow lead over Netanyahu's Likud. To form a government, Yashar or Likud will need to cobble together a 61-seat majority of parties to be able to form a new coalition government. TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE Who is the 66-year-old Eisenkot? He was born in Tiberias in Israel’s north to a Jewish-Moroccan family who relocated to Israel’s southernmost city, Eilat, on the Red Sea when he was a toddler. A career soldier, he opted to serve in the infantry. He was part of the elite Golani Brigade and reached the zenith of the military with his 2015 appointment to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) chief of staff in 2015 until 2019. Yossi Melman, one of Israel’s most respected journalists on intelligence and defense reporting, told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot, "Is 100% a soldier. He is very brave and humble. He is an officer and gentleman." Melman noted that when Eisenkot was chosen to be the next IDF chief of staff, he declined because he felt that then General Benny Gantz should receive the appointment. Melman asked, "How many people would do that? He was selected after Gantz. It shows his traits of modesty, honesty and not arrogant." Melman said, "It is a miracle he is leading in the polls. He is the antithesis of a what a politician should be. He is not a great orator when you compare him to Netanyahu. He radiates honesty." BENJAMIN NETANYAHU'S LEGACY AND POLITICAL FUTURE ON THE LINE IN ISRAEL'S OCT 27 ELECTION Eisenkot’s Mizrahi background — Jews who originate from North Africa and the Middle East — would mean, if he prevails, that he would be the first Israeli Prime Minister of Moroccan origin. The Prime Minister’s office has been held by Israelis of Eastern European descent (Ashkenazi) since the rebirth of the Jewish state in 1948. After Hamas invaded Israel on Oct. 7, 2023 and slaughtered over 1,200 people, including more than 40 Americans, Eisenkot joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet as a minister without portfolio. Melman said Eisenkot "did not set any political conditions" and "his presence in the cabinet saved Netanyahu." After eight months of serving in the war cabinet, Eisenkot resigned, blaming the prime minister for failing to implement a comprehensive strategy. The war against the Iran-backed terrorist movement Hamas took an enormous toll on the battle-hardened General Eisenkot and his family. Hamas killed his son, 25-year-old Master Sergeant Gal Eisenkot, in Dec. 2023. The terrorist organization also killed two nephews of Eisenkot. Netanyahu and his wife Sara said at the time that they were devastated by Gal’s death and Eisenkot was a "true hero." ZIONISM EXPLAINED FROM ITS BIBLICAL ORIGINS TO THE REBIRTH OF THE STATE OF ISRAEL Danny Orbach, a military historian from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, gave his take on the leading contender to replace Netanyahu. "I think his military record and his prospects as a national leader have both significant strengths and serious weaknesses. He bears considerable responsibility for shaping the IDF that existed on Oct. 7, 2023. And that was, paradoxically, both the army that proved capable of defeating Hezbollah, striking Iran and achieving unprecedented military successes in the extraordinarily difficult, tunnel-ridden battlefield of Gaza and the army that failed so miserably on Oct. 7." He continued that, "Like other chiefs of staff, Eisenkot bears responsibility for the decisions that reduced the army's size and for the infamous ‘conceptzia’ [Hebrew word for concept] regarding Hamas. In that respect, I consider him just as culpable as Netanyahu." Israel’s military, intelligence and political establishments bought into the ‘conceptzia’ that Hamas could be housebroken with massive infusions of economic aid. Hamas, however, was wedded to its radical Islamist ideology —the destruction of the Jewish state — and used the funds to advance its war aims. Orbach noted that "I don't think most of Eisenkot's support stems from his energy, enthusiasm or even his political platform. My impression is that Eisenkot has emerged as the default ‘non-Bibi’ candidate, the politician who currently channels much of the camp's hopes and expectations." Orbach added that "I also doubt that Eisenkot would have had the political determination to stand up to the Biden administration on such matters." Netanyahu and former President Biden repeatedly clashed over Biden’s attempts to rope in Israel’s efforts to defeat Iran’s seven-front war against the Jewish state. The military historian, however, noted that "I believe an Eisenkot government could address several of Israel's most urgent problems. It would remove Ben Gvir from power, confront the growing problem of Jewish extremist violence and terrorism in the West Bank, and begin repairing Israel's severely damaged international legitimacy." Itamar Ben-Gvir is a controversial right-wing firebrand politician and the current minister of national security since 2022, who has outraged many Western European and foreign leaders with his heated rhetoric against the Palestinians. TIMELINE OF DECADES-LONG ISRAELI-ARAB, PALESTINIAN CONFLICT Eisenkot’s wife, Hannah, comes from an American Jewish family. U.S. General Joseph Dunford awarded Eisenkot the Commander of the Legion of Merit because of his "exceptionally meritorious service as chief of the General Staff of the IDF" and his "contribution to the strategic cooperation between the United States and Israel [that] will have a lasting effect on both countries," according to the Washington Institute, where Eisenkot served as a military fellow in 2019. Nadav Eyal, an Israeli analyst and journalist for the mass circulation Israeli paper Yedioth Aharonoth, told Fox News Digital, Gadi Eisenkot is widely considered one of the most successful Chiefs of Staff that Israel has had in the last thirty years." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP He continued that "Chiefs of Staff in Israel, unlike in other countries, are really extremely capable, in general, to be prime minister. They are leading the country’s biggest organization, the IDF." Eyal, who writes extensively about the IDF, credited Eisenkot’s military planning against the Iran-backed Hezbollah terrorist organization in Lebanon and the significant defeats the Lebanese Shiite entity experienced, including the "discovery of tunnels that Hezbollah built" to enter Israel. Hezbollah immediately joined Hamas’s war against Israel in Oct. 2023. Given the nature of Israel’s electoral system, an outright winner won’t likely be known for several days, since the leading party will need to form a coalition to get to the 61-seat mandate to run the country.

articles.title: In 2023, Natalie Portman bought a 1912 Paris mansion that once served as an embassy for €15.2 million; the 550-square-metre home near the Eiffel Tower had been restored with a garden, gym and glass-roofed reception room
articles.summary: Hollywood actress Natalie Portman, who relocated from Los Angeles to Paris long ago, has bought a 550-square-metre mansion in the French capital for €15.2
articles.body: Hollywood actress Natalie Portman, who relocated from Los Angeles to Paris long ago, has bought a 550-square-metre mansion in the French capital for €15.2 million. The four-storey property bought by the actor in 2023 was built in 1912, and had previously served as an embassy before being turned into a private residence. The property is located not far from the iconic Eiffel Tower. According to Architectural Digest, it comprises a garden, gym, library, wine cellar, and a reception room covered by a glass roof. The house underwent a major renovation before Portman bought it.The purchase was reported by French publication Madame Figaroin in 2024, citing an earlier report by Challenges. Portman's property is located in the Champ-de-Mars area, close to one of Paris's best-known landmarks. Although the actress had already spent several years living in the French capital, this purchase gave her a separate residence in a neighbourhood where she had previously rented an apartment.The transaction took place months before Portman and her former husband, French choreographer Benjamin Millepied, finalised their divorce in February 2024. The couple had lived in Paris with their two children after moving to the city in 2016. Their rented apartment was only a short distance from the mansion that Portman later bought.What makes the property different from many other celebrity homes is its past. It was not originally built as a modern luxury residence. Over more than a century, the building had been used for different purposes, including as an embassy in the 1980s. Its transformation into a private mansion came later, following a change in ownership and extensive restoration work.How a former embassy became a luxury residenceThe building's renovation was carried out under French businessman Yves Vatelot, who acquired it in the 1990s. Vatelot, an entrepreneur associated with the wine industry, oversaw the restoration of the property, which eventually became a four-storey private home.According to Architectural Digest France, the mansion retained several features associated with its original architecture even after being modernised. Among them is a wrought-iron staircase connecting the floors. A lift was also installed, providing another way to move between the different levels of the house.The property was subsequently offered for sale through French real estate agency Philippe Menager-Nicolas Hug.The renovation also gave different floors their own functions. The mansion contains separate areas for exercise, reading, entertaining guests and spending time outdoors.What is inside Natalie Portman's €15.2 million home?One of the main features of the house is a reception room on the fourth floor. Unlike a conventional living room, this space has a glass roof that allows daylight to enter from above. Photographs released by the property agency show the room beneath the glass structure, with views of the surrounding city available from the upper level.The mansion also has a gym on the ground floor. Other facilities include a library and a wine cellar, along with a dining area and several private rooms. The interiors were designed to retain the character of the older building while providing the facilities of a modern residence.The mansion also includes a patio, garden and terrace, giving its occupants access to open areas despite its central Paris location. The terrace provides views across the French capital.The four floors are connected by both the staircase and the lift. With a total area of 550 square metres, the property has enough space to accommodate its various facilities.Why the location is significantPortman's mansion stands in Paris's seventh arrondissement, an area that includes the Eiffel Tower and the Champ-de-Mars gardens. The neighbourhood is known for its historic properties and has attracted several wealthy international residents.Other prominent property owners in the area include Morocco's King Mohammed VI, WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum and French property developer Olivier Mitterrand, who is the nephew of former French President François Mitterrand.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft founded an anti-hate organisation in 2019; its October 21 New York gala raised more than $32 million in one night, drawing Tom Brady, Jon Bon Jovi and over 800 guests
articles.summary: More than 800 guests gathered at New York’s Waldorf Astoria on October 21, 2026, for an evening that combined celebrity appearances, philanthropy and a
articles.body: More than 800 guests gathered at New York’s Waldorf Astoria on October 21, 2026, for an evening that combined celebrity appearances, philanthropy and a campaign against antisemitism and discrimination. The inaugural benefit gala of the Blue Square Alliance Against Hate, founded by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, raised more than $32 million, according to the organisation’s official announcement published on October 23. The fundraising total marked the largest amount the organisation had raised in a single night. Former Patriots quarterback Tom Brady, musician Jon Bon Jovi and prominent business and community leaders attended the event, which also honoured Bank of America chairman and CEO Brian Moynihan for his support of the organisation’s mission.How Robert Kraft’s anti-hate initiative beganKraft founded the organisation in 2019 as the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism. It was established to encourage Americans to confront antisemitism and support Jewish communities, using public awareness campaigns and partnerships to reach people who might not otherwise engage with the issue. In 2025, the organisation adopted the name Blue Square Alliance Against Hate, reflecting an expanded effort to build a broader coalition against antisemitism and other forms of hate. The blue square became its central symbol of solidarity, allowing people from different backgrounds to visibly express their support for the cause.The organisation says its approach combines mass-media campaigns, social content, partnerships, coalition-building and data analysis. Its goal is to encourage people to move beyond passive agreement and actively challenge prejudice when they encounter it.Gala brings together sports, entertainment and business leadersThe sold-out event featured a guest list spanning professional sports, music, business, religion and public life. Brady joined Kraft and Cardinal Timothy Dolan, the archbishop emeritus of New York, on stage, while Bon Jovi was among the notable attendees. Disturbed frontman David Draiman, CNN journalists Wolf Blitzer and Bianna Golodryga, New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch and New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin were also present.CNN commentator Van Jones opened the programme, while former US secretary of state Condoleezza Rice delivered a video message about her experiences confronting racism and hate. The evening recognised Moynihan for his support of the organisation’s work. He also serves as chair of its first advisory board, which brings together leaders from business, media, diplomacy and law.The blue square symbol was a recurring feature throughout the gathering, appearing on guests’ clothing as a visible expression of solidarity. The event aimed to demonstrate how influential people and institutions could use their platforms to encourage a wider public response to hate.Why the $32 million fundraising total mattersThe more than $32 million raised at the gala represents a major fundraising milestone for the organisation. According to its official announcement, the proceeds will support the continued expansion of its programmes, including its Command Center technology and analytics, national media and advertising campaigns, and initiatives such as Stand Up Sunday and the Unity Dinner series.The organisation’s Command Center supports its research and data-driven work, while its media campaigns seek to reach audiences through familiar cultural platforms. Its strategy reflects the belief that awareness alone may not be enough to change behaviour, and that accessible messages can help encourage people to intervene when they encounter antisemitism or other forms of prejudice.The gala also followed the organisation’s Stand Up Sunday initiative, conducted in partnership with the Appeal of Conscience Foundation. The initiative brought together more than two million Americans from different faith communities in a nationwide expression of solidarity against antisemitism and religious hate, according to the alliance.Super Bowl advertisements help spread its messageOne of the organisation’s most visible strategies has been using major sporting events and popular culture to bring the fight against antisemitism to a broader audience. Its Super Bowl advertisements have helped introduce the blue square campaign to millions of viewers beyond traditional community networks.A 2024 advertisement featured a former speechwriter for Martin Luther King Jr. encouraging viewers to stand up to antisemitism. In 2025, a commercial featuring Brady and rapper Snoop Dogg broadened the message to opposition to hate of all kinds. A subsequent campaign, titled “Sticky Note”, depicted a Jewish student facing bullying and a Black classmate covering an antisemitic slur on his backpack with a blue square.The campaigns reflect Kraft’s stated belief that confronting antisemitism can also help build resistance to other forms of prejudice. The alliance has sought to turn the blue square into a recognisable symbol that people can wear, share and use to demonstrate support.A broader coalition against hateThe gala’s fundraising achievement comes amid continuing concerns about antisemitism in the United States. The Anti-Defamation League recorded 9,354 antisemitic incidents nationwide in 2024, its highest annual total since it began tracking such incidents 46 years ago. For the Blue Square Alliance, the challenge is to turn public attention and financial support into sustained engagement. Its work extends from awareness campaigns to educational initiatives and partnerships designed to encourage people from different backgrounds to stand against discrimination.The October 21 gathering brought together prominent figures from several sectors around that objective. With more than $32 million raised in one night, the organisation now has additional resources to expand its campaigns and partnerships. The longer-term measure of success will be whether that investment helps more people recognise prejudice, challenge antisemitism and take action against hate in their communities.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed Ukraine Starlink ‘loophole’ after limits hit drone operations
articles.summary: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations.
articles.body: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations. Ukraine said Saturday that both Starlink, run by Musk’s SpaceX, and its military variant Starshield were now fully functional after the long outage, two days after President Donald Trump indicated Musk had been asked to “put it back.” In a series of posts on X on Saturday night into Sunday morning, Musk accused Ukraine of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using it for offensive drone strikes. “That loophole was closed last week,” the billionaire wrote. “Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” he added. In a separate post, he said: “We simply enforced our terms of service when they were bypassed.” SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither Musk nor the United States government ​had initially taken responsibility for imposing the curbs last week, with Musk saying with respect to Starshield that “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.” Starlink technology has been critical to frontline communications and Ukraine’s ability to intercept jet-powered drones since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of the country in 2022. Ukraine does not rely on the systems for long-range drone operations within Russia, though it is used for military operations in Ukrainian territories unlawfully annexed by Russia. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions were imposed without warning and capped Starshield operations at speeds of 100 mph, hampering the military’s ability to intercept drones and forcing the cancellation of some operations. “Starlink remains critical to the defense of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now,” Musk said. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.” In a series of posts and replies, he called his critics “bloodthirsty warmongers” who “want the war to continue until every last man in Ukraine has died in a ditch.” Hours later, responding to an X user comment that said “Zelensky needs to go,” Musk responded: “Yes.” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Starlink speeds started returning to normal on Saturday night. Ukraine’s defense ministry said Saturday that the connection remained stable at over 250mph. The Ukrainian military does not disclose the systems’ maximum operating speeds. Russia has barraged Ukraine over the past week, Zelenskyy said on Sunday, though he did not draw any direct link to the limitations. “This past week alone, Russia has launched around 1,600 guided aerial bombs, 48 missiles of various types, including ballistic missiles, and nearly 2,300 attack drones against Ukraine. Unfortunately, almost every day, these brutal strikes leave people killed and injured,” he said in a post on X. The restrictions on Starlink services last week came amid a souring of relations between the White House and Ukraine, after President Donald Trump agreed to a diesel deal with Russia, waived sweeping sanctions, and called for Ukraine to get a new president. In a response to Musk on Sunday, Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said Sunday that “It’s very strange that Elon Musk doesn’t know about the restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine.” “Starlink does not work over Russian territory,” he said in a post on Telegram. “So we PHYSICALLY CANNOT USE COMMERCIAL STARLINK for deep strikes and mid-range strikes.” The disruptions to the Starlink service coincided with what Ukrainian officials described as a temporary interruption to U.S. intelligence warnings about incoming Russian attacks. Zelenskyy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” last week that U.S. intelligence sharing was briefly “blocked,” blinding Ukraine to incoming ballistic missiles. Asked whether he thought Trump or Musk had directly made the decision to limit Starlink, Zelenskyy said he did not know but thought “both” were involved. He said that if Trump decided tomorrow to lift the restriction, “it will immediately work as it was before.” Asked whether he spoke to Musk on Thursday, Trump said: “I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference, I guess. The bottom line — he put it back.” Before the latest collapse in relations with Washington, Ukraine’s military had been chipping away at land seized by Russia in the eastern Donetsk region, part of the Donbas heartland that the Kremlin has been struggling to fully capture. In one major operation, more than 100 square miles of territory and 16 settlements have been reclaimed, Ukrainian officials have said, crediting methods like using bomber drones to fly robot vehicles behind enemy lines.

articles.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
articles.summary: Nayib Bukele says bodies delivered to soldiers are "not our men" amid search for Salvadorans abducted last week.
articles.body:
Four bodies handed over to special forces on a mission to Haiti to recover Salvadoran hostages are "not our men", El Salvador's president has said.

Nayib Bukele said a nongovernmental organisation delivered the human remains to one of Haiti's airports claiming they were four El Salvadoran air technicians, but that one of the corpses was a child's and another was wearing a different country's army uniform.

He had dispatched a military contingent, reportedly of hundreds of soldiers, on Thursday after the four men vanished after being ambushed by "heavily armed criminal groups".

The hostages had been part of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), which is tasked with tackling worsening gang violence in Haiti.

The men had been travelling back to their camp in an armoured vehicle when they were attacked in an area of the Caribbean island nation controlled by armed groups called Croix-des-Bouquets. No gang has so far claimed responsibility.

Bukele previously said the Salvadoran military operation in Haiti had the sole purpose of returning the four men alive. Approximately 450 soldiers had so far been deployed, according to Haitian newspaper Le Nouvelliste.

Bukele said the bodies the mission had received included one of a man of "considerably greater height than that of our air technicians", a person "who was wearing part of a uniform from an army that is not ours", and that among the remains were identification cards and uniforms from other countries.

He posted pictures showing the ID card of a GSF member and a corresponding national ID card from Chad in Africa.

Bukele's comments poured skepticism on an earlier report in the New York Times, citing people close to the Salvadoran mission, that the bodies found on the outskirts of the Haitian capital, Port-au-Prince, on Saturday were thought to belong to the missing men.

The newspaper reported that the bodies delivered to the military contingent had been badly burned, meaning a medical examination would be required to identify them.

It cited one unnamed source briefed on the situation as saying the ID posted by Bukele in fact belonged to a soldier who had lost it when he had been injured.

Haiti has been ravaged by gang violence for years, but the situation has worsened in the political vacuum that followed the assassination of its president in 2021.

The multinational force dispatched to quell the violence and push back the armed gangs has struggled to penetrate areas where they hold sway.

More than 5,700 people have been killed or injured by gangs or during operations against them between 1 January and 11 September this year, the UN said at the start of October.

Bukele said the four GSF members had primarily been there to "carry out medical evacuations and save lives, not to wage war".

When they were abducted, helicopters were deployed and multiple attempts were made to reach the location, but these efforts were hampered by fighting in the area, the Salvadoran armed forces said.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO wants a wealth tax, but Americans deserve to keep their legacy
articles.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby's call for a near-100% inheritance tax sparks fierce debate over property rights and the American Dream.
articles.body: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby advocates for a national wealth tax and an inheritance tax approaching 100% on amounts exceeding a threshold. My response is simple: Washington should not become the principal beneficiary of the American Dream. According to reporting highlighted by Fox Business, Kirby believes wealth inequality requires a national response. He has every right to make that argument. But a proposal to confiscate nearly everything above a government-determined threshold deserves a forceful challenge. LET SOCIALISTS ROB FROM THE RICH 100% AND YOU STILL WON’T BE ABLE TO PAY THE BILLS The ability to build something and leave it to your family is one of the most powerful incentives in our economy. Treating that aspiration as a social problem would send America in precisely the wrong direction. As the founder of Engineered Tax Services, I have spent my career working with people who build businesses, invest in communities and create jobs. Their wealth often exists in operating companies, buildings, equipment and ownership interests. Those assets are productive — and frequently illiquid. NEWSOM BEGS CALIFORNIANS TO VOTE 'NO' ON BILLIONAIRE'S TAX IN FACE OF MASS EXODUS, PITCHES NATIONWIDE TAX HIKE A business valuation does not mean a business owner has that amount sitting in a checking account. Yet an annual wealth tax could demand cash based on an estimated asset value, even when the owner has received no corresponding income. Where does the money come from? Depending on the rules, owners could have to borrow, sell assets or withdraw capital from their businesses. Money that might have funded equipment, expansion or hiring could instead go toward paying a tax on continued ownership. Supporters must explain why that tradeoff would serve the workers whose opportunities depend on those investments. FORMER WASHINGTON GOVERNOR RIPS HER OWN PARTY FOR PUSHING MILLIONAIRES OUT The inheritance proposal raises an even more fundamental question: Who should decide what happens to a lifetime of work? Parents often sacrifice because they want their children to have greater security and opportunity. Entrepreneurs take risks knowing that success could benefit their families long after they are gone. That motivation deserves respect — and drives real economic growth. Kirby reportedly has not specified the threshold at which inheritance taxes should approach 100%. That omission matters. Nobody should pretend his remarks establish a detailed proposal affecting every family business. THE DSA’S DANGEROUS FINE PRINT. THEY'RE COMING FOR MILLIONAIRES (AND YOU) But even at an extremely high threshold, the principle remains troubling. A near-total marginal tax would give government an overwhelming claim on the portion of an estate above its chosen limit. Why should Washington have a stronger claim to that property than the people its owner chooses to support? Why should an arbitrary number set by the government determine the extent of one person’s property rights relative to another’s? Advocates will argue that inherited wealth can entrench privilege. That concern deserves a serious response. Birth should never determine the limits of a person's opportunity. But neither should the government. DAVID MARCUS: WHY ABDUL EL-SAYED’S ANTI-BILLIONAIRE SCREEDS MAY NOT PLAY IN GRAND RAPIDS Confiscating a successful family's legacy does not, by itself, equip another family to build one. And elected officials don’t have a great track record when it comes to managing budgets and programs. A business valuation does not mean a business owner has that amount sitting in a checking account. Yet an annual wealth tax could demand cash based on an estimated asset value, even when the owner has received no corresponding income. Where does the money come from? We should judge policy by whether it helps more Americans become owners: start a company, purchase property, acquire useful skills, secure financing and accumulate savings. CONSERVATIVES CAN FIGHT THE RISE OF SOCIALISM BY DEFENDING THE AMERICAN FAMILY That is where my commitment to tax equality comes from. Too many small businesses lack access to the expertise, incentives and opportunities that sophisticated organizations know how to use. Expanding that access offers a practical path toward broader prosperity. Also, be honest about taxation: Some accumulated wealth reflects income already taxed; some reflects appreciation that has not yet been taxed. Sound reasoning against confiscatory taxation does not require pretending every dollar has the same history. It requires recognizing that taxes change incentives — and that property rights should remain meaningful even when an owner becomes extraordinarily successful. Kirby's reported willingness to pay these taxes himself does not settle the issue. Public policy must account for people with different assets, obligations and circumstances. One executive's willingness cannot substitute for a workable national policy. America needs vigorous competition, fewer barriers to business formation and more pathways to financial independence. We should challenge special favors that protect incumbents and make it harder for newcomers to compete. And we should demand that government demonstrate discipline with the resources it already receives before granting it sweeping new claims on private wealth. The American promise is that effort, risk and perseverance can create something lasting. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION We should strengthen that promise for families still trying to get ahead. articles.title: Brazil becomes next test for Latin America’s surging conservative movement
articles.summary: Lula da Silva seeks a fourth presidential term in Brazil in a closely contested second round election with Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as security and safety concerns weigh heavily.
articles.body: Brazil's estimated 158 million voters could advance Latin America's conservative wave in Sunday's election as the continent's most populous nation could elect conservative Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro as its next president. The first round election three weeks ago saw a strong performance by Bolsonaro, proving the polls wrong. While incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (Lula) had been predicted to take the first round by single digits, Bolsonaro ended up winning 47% to Lula's 45%. As neither candidate won a majority, the election went to a second round. Brazil's election follows a long string of victories for the Latin American right across Central and South America that started with the election of Libertarian outsider Javier Milei in Argentina in 2023. BOLSONARO WINS FIRST ROUND OF BRAZILIAN PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION, AS TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATES CONTINUE RED WAVE 2025 saw a right-wing sweep across the region, as Ecuador, Bolivia, Honduras and Chile all voted for conservative heads of state. In 2026, Keiko Fujimori narrowly defeated a left-wing candidate to win the Peruvian presidency, while most recently, in Colombia, conservative attorney Abelardo de la Espriella bested left-wing Senator Ivan Cepeda. Bolsonaro's slate of congressional candidates also fared well, ensuring that Brazil will have one of the most conservative congresses in years, and a legislative branch aligned with Bolsonaro's goals, or ready to thwart Lula's agenda. The two candidates met Friday night for the final debate in Rio de Janeiro, which featured a series of questions organized around Brazil's five geographic regions. While the debate featured some heated personal exchanges, it appears unlikely to have moved the needle in either direction heading into a close race. TRUMP'S WAR ON DRUG CARTELS COULD GAIN POWERFUL NEW ALLY AFTER PIVOTAL ELECTION President Donald Trump has heralded these electoral results as vindication for his hardline approach to security, crime, and migration policies, as well as a stamp of approval for the new Shield of the Americas initiative. The Trump administration counts on considerably more close allies now than it did at the beginning of Trump's second term. Yet, the question remains: why is the region resoundingly rejecting the left and progressivism? Many of the elections have been won by narrow margins, with Brazil being a case in point: Lula bested Jair Bolsonaro in 2022 by just 1.8%. While many Latin American nations remain deeply polarized, there is no denying a right-wing resurgence. Commentators appear to be expressing a rejection of progressive movements amid growing concerns over safety and security, giving approval to proposals to dramatically ramp up police and military presence to combat crime and drug trafficking. Meanwhile, leftist parties seem unable to capitalize on recurring concerns over inflation and kitchen table economics, which have played into the hands of the Latin American right, as working class and middle class voters have felt the pinch of rising food, housing and energy costs. In addition to social and economic concerns, the specter of Jair Bolsonaro also looms over the election. Flavio Bolsonaro has pledged to free his father, who is currently serving a 27-year sentence on house arrest for allegedly plotting a coup in the wake of the 2022 election. Lula was also sentenced to a 12-year prison sentence on corruption charges stemming from the infamous Operation Car Wash, until he was freed on a technicality by the Brazilian Supreme Court, and rose from the ashes to win the 2022 presidential election. BRAZIL’S RAPID ELECTION COUNT PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON VOTING SECURITY AHEAD OF US MIDTERMS Bolsonaro has narrowly led in recent polls, and enters the second round with some structural advantages. Most importantly, he enjoys the backing of three of the four other major candidates in the race, who failed to advance to the second round. Self-help author Augusto Cury, former Goias Governor Ronaldo Caiado, and former Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema all officially backed Bolsonaro in the second round. Entrepreneur Renan Santos, candidate for the Mission Party, declined to endorse either candidate. However, as his political movement is characterized as free-market and libertarian, these voters are also more likely to trend to Bolsonaro. Thus, Lula needs to win a significant majority of first round voters who backed right-wing or center-right candidates. It's a daunting, but not impossible, proposition. The entire election may hinge on voters who are voting against a candidate, as much as for a candidate. Another question looming over the election: has Lula finally worn out his welcome with the Brazilian electorate? This will be Lula's seventh time in 40 years appearing on a presidential ballot: he lost elections in 1989, 1994, 1998, won in 2002, 2006, and 2022. Lula famously promised to serve only one term when he ran to oust Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. On October 25, 2022, just five days before the last second round presidential election, he posted on his official X account: "If elected, I will be a single-term president." It was a promise that he did not keep. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Various polls have shown that voters are not happy with the course of Lula's third term, and even a sizable percentage of Lula backers in 2022 responded with pessimism on the prospect of an unprecedented fourth term. However, a large percentage of the Brazilian electorate also consistently rejects the prospect of voting for another Bolsonaro for president. Lula is unquestionably the dominant figure in Brazilian politics over the past half-century. But will his magnetism and charisma be enough to overcome the right-wing resurgence sweeping the continent?

articles.title: Young woman joked about going missing — 10 years later, mom won't rest until she finds out who killed her
articles.summary: Angie Barlow vanished after texting her roommate about a private party gig in Indianapolis. Her mother says prosecutors have gone silent on the case.
articles.body: As an Indiana mother continues to search for answers in her daughter’s unsolved murder, she says it has been years without answers from Indianapolis prosecutors. For Angie Barlow’s mother, Christina Kramer, the 10-year mark of her daughter’s disappearance brings questions about both her death and the status of the ongoing investigation. Angie Barlow, 23, disappeared on Oct. 26, 2016, after texting her roommate the address of a private dancing gig at the Landmark Apartment and Townhomes in Indianapolis. GABBY PETITO'S MOTHER URGES PUBLIC 'RIPPLE EFFECT' TO HELP FIND THE MISSING 5 YEARS AFTER DAUGHTER'S MURDER "About to work this private party in case I go missing LOL," the text message read, Kramer told Fox News Digital. Nearly eight months later, searchers found Barlow’s remains in a backyard of a residence off Harcourt in Indianapolis, WISH-TV reported. Kramer said her daughter had been fatally shot. TEEN FOUND IN SHALLOW CALIFORNIA VINEYARD GRAVE IDENTIFIED NEARLY 50 YEARS LATER AS FAMILY WARNS KILLER Kramer added that she is desperate for answers after a special prosecutor assigned to the case left the office. She estimated it had been around two years since she has heard from the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office. "I had been sending a bunch of emails for I don't even know how long to absolutely nobody," Kramer told Fox News Digital, adding that she no longer has a point of contact with the prosecutor’s office. JONBENET RAMSEY'S DAD PRESSES FOR NEW LAW IN DECADES-LONG HUNT FOR DAUGHTER’S KILLER Kramer said she has also tried repeatedly to reach Marion County Prosecuting Attorney Ryan Mears but has not received a response. The Marion County Prosecutor's Office did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Fox News Digital. Surveillance footage and GPS tracker Kramer said surveillance footage from the apartment complex showed two vehicles leaving at around 3:30 a.m. on Oct. 27, 2016. She identified one vehicle as Barlow's blue Pontiac G6. A black sedan followed closely behind, believed to have belonged to a female acquaintance who worked with Barlow at Club Rio in Indianapolis, Kramer said. The footage did not allow investigators to identify the drivers or occupants because of the vehicles' tinted windows, WISH-TV reported. Kramer said days went by without answers. She then contacted the dealership where Barlow purchased the vehicle and used its GPS tracker to help locate it around eight miles from the apartment complex. While Barlow normally kept her car meticulously clean, Kramer said the recovered vehicle had been completely trashed inside and looked as though it had been driven under a fence. "That car had been on some kind of journey," Kramer added. Alleged taunts Kramer said months later, she received a phone call from the acquaintance who had been at the private party with her boyfriend. Kramer said that Barlow knew the pair, but they were not friends. "She needed some quick cash, and this was the way to do it," Kramer said, adding that she would have never accepted the gig had she known who was there. During the Jan. 2017 call, Kramer recalled asking the female acquaintance what she and Barlow had discussed at the party. "Oh, you want to know what her last words were," Kramer recalled the woman saying. Kramer said the remark stayed with her because she interpreted it as a taunt. The woman denied making the call and having that conversation, according to what Kramer told Fox News Digital. The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department said that no criminal charges have been filed in Barlow’s death. IMPD told Fox News Digital that the investigation remains open with Detective Jose Torres as the lead investigator but declined to comment further. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X ‘I'm her voice’ Despite standing less than 5 feet tall, Barlow excelled as a softball catcher, her mother said. She also competed in basketball, shot put, volleyball and bowling. "She was a very gifted athlete. There was not a sport that she did not do," Kramer said. "Whenever I talk about her, especially the good things, it just, it makes you happy." She was the eldest of four sisters, whom she remained close to after she left the family’s Muncie home. SEND US A TIP Kramer said she will continue pressing authorities to solve her daughter's murder. GOT A TIP? "When you remain silent, you're a victim. When you have a voice, you're a survivor, and I refuse to be a victim of my circumstances," Kramer said. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "My daughter was the victim. She can't speak for herself. I'm her survivor. I'm her voice, and I speak for her." articles.title: MIKE DAVIS: Shocking $6M verdict shows why DOJ must investigate MIT
articles.summary: A jury awarded David Sabatini $6 million after rejecting sexual-misconduct claims that ended his MIT career and shuttered his Whitehead lab.
articles.body: A Massachusetts jury recently awarded scientist David Sabatini $6 million and rejected the sexual-misconduct claims that had ended his career at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and shuttered his research laboratory at the Whitehead Institute. The jury’s seven women and six men brought a measure of objectivity and decency to the facts that the leaders of MIT and Whitehead could not. Sabatini’s case is a perfect example how DEI and the rest of the left’s political crusades are so destructive to America. The verdict vindicates Sabatini, who has long maintained that his accuser, Kristin Knouse, had lied. But the legal fight took years of his life and nearly ruined him financially. And it shouldn’t be the end of the story. The trial exposed how thin — and how rotten — MIT’s and Whitehead’s case against Sabatini had been all along. MIT and Whitehead owe the public a reckoning. The Trump administration must investigate MIT and Whitehead. Before 2021, scientists revered Sabatini as one of the greatest molecular cell biologists alive. He ran a major lab at Whitehead, held a professorship at MIT, served as a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator and received tens of millions of dollars in federal funding. Sabatini’s " groundbreaking " research could yield new cancer and aging therapies and save countless lives. Predictions swirled that he’d one day win the Nobel Prize. It all came crashing down. Evidence at trial shows that Knouse — who led her own lab — launched a campaign she termed "covert operation dethrone" to topple Sabatini after he ended their roughly year-and-a-half-long relationship. She messaged one friend that Sabatini was going to be "Weinstein’ed out of science" ; another that she was "out for blood." Knouse told colleagues that Sabatini had harassed and assaulted her, and in the fall of 2020 took her claims to Whitehead’s new director, Ruth Lehmann. Lehmann proved an eager audience. After one meeting, Knouse reported that Lehmann acted "as if she wants a formal reason to fire" Sabatini. After another meeting, Lehmann "indicated she plans to fire him." "If I don’t do this," Lehmann reportedly said , "how can anyone ever believe I’m committed to changing this place?" Lehmann denied making the comments in a later deposition. Whitehead eventually hired a law firm to conduct an investigation, but later reporting and trial evidence indicate the investigation had a largely predetermined outcome. The firm’s final report reached no conclusion on whether Sabatini’s and Knouse’s relationship had been consensual. Mostly it faulted Sabatini for not reporting his relationship with Knouse to HR and for a "sexualized undercurrent" in his lab –an environment which it deemed, along with the relationship, to violate an anti-harassment policy. Perhaps most shocking, though, the report took umbrage with Sabatini’s focus on "science above all else" and his "propensity" to "praise or gravitate" toward those demonstrating "scientific success." The fallout was immediate. The Howard Hughes Medical Institute quickly fired Sabatini; that same day, after Whitehead told him it would dismiss him, he resigned. Which might leave you wondering: Did administrators have no sense of proportionality, no sense of the gravity of removing Sabatini — that it would wreck not just one man and one career but an entire research ecosystem? But then it’s always easier to destroy than create. Lehmann was, after all, a DEI warrior. She ranked "diversity and disparities," alongside research, as one of the areas most "important for science." As Whitehead director, she hired DEI officers and instituted a new DEI Council, DEI Seminar Series, DEI Heritage Email series, and an internship program targeting "historically underrepresented groups." And she oversaw both a DEI strategic plan that pledged to hire "diverse talent" and the publication of Whitehead’s first DEI report, which touted the "increasing diversity in our community" alongside statistics showing a decrease in the percentage of white employees between 2020 and 2022. After Sabatini’s removal from Whitehead, Nergis Mavalvala, MIT’s dean of science, was part of a three-member committee that convened to consider his tenure at MIT. It was a solemn assignment: revocations of tenure anywhere are exceedingly rare, and there’s no public record of a single case ever at MIT. Nevertheless, Mavalvala testified at trial that the committee hadn’t spoken to any former members of Sabatini’s lab about the veracity of the accusations against him — including the 34 who had written in his support. In early 2022, the committee recommended that MIT revoke Sabatini’s tenure. Under intense pressure, Sabatini resigned. What explains the committee’s actions? Here, too, trial evidence is damning. On the day Whitehead gave Sabatini the law firm’s report, Mavalvala wrote to Lehmann about its contents and assured her that "there is complete alignment between our viewpoints on this whole sordid affair." She then added : "I find myself say[ing] ‘Yeah, go Ruth!’ almost every time you speak. You are at the vanguard of cultural change, and that is never easy or quick." Cultural change . Not the pursuit of science. Not academic excellence. Not moral leadership. Her later emails heap exuberant praise on the Whitehead director, with lines such as : "OMG, you are a trailblazer Ruth." On the stand, Mavalvala said that her committee’s investigation into Sabatini was unbiased and independent of Whitehead. Questioned about her emails, she retorted that her "alignment" with Lehmann concerned processes only, not the desired outcome of Sabatini’s case. The jury laughed. In the end, 13 ordinary citizens from a deep-blue state humiliated MIT and Whitehead by upholding due process and the dignity of every individual — regardless of race or gender. Their verdict is the latest sign that public trust in our academic institutions has collapsed. So what next? Thanks to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Fair Admissions v. Harvard and the Trump administration’s crackdown on unlawful DEI practices, Whitehead has purged its website of materials that once touted its diversity initiatives. But insiders report that DEI is alive and well. Sabatini now runs a lab in Prague and, more recently, a Czech-affiliated one in Boston. To satisfy the demands of wokeness, America gave Europe one of our best scientists. Knouse directs a lab at MIT, and the National Institutes of Health recently awarded her a large grant. Lehmann and Mavalvala continue in their posts. And neither MIT nor Whitehead has signaled any willingness to examine its conduct regarding Sabatini, to reconsider his employment, or to sanction anyone involved in this debacle. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP MIT and Whitehead receive over a billion dollars annually in taxpayer funds. The public deserves an accounting of whether MIT and Whitehead used our money to further "cultural change," the degradation of science, and the ruin of a man on a sham pretext. An investigation into the weaponization of DEI would right a deep wrong and signal a return to an America-first pursuit of scientific excellence. It would send the message that we should level our condemnation not against scientists who pursue "science above all else," but against those who offer little but destruction in the name of progress.
